📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You Must Remember This is a podcast dedicated, as its host Karina Longworth says in every intro, to exploring the secret and/or forgotten histories of Hollywood’s first century. Longworth, who is an LA–based writer and film preservationist, usually tells her stories in themed seasons. Those include Erotic 90’s, spanning the introduction of the NC-17 rating to Eyes Wide Shut; Dead Blondes (Marilyn Monroe, Jean Harlow, Veronica Lake); and a whole series exploring the web of connections Charles Manson had to Hollywood. It’s addictive, exhaustively researched, and narrated in a way that is both soothing and trancelike.

Recent findings suggest that longworth is a native Angeleno who has been writing about film for years. She was a film editor and critic at the LA Weekly for three years until 2012; wrote books on Al Pacino and Meryl Streep; and then started You Must Remember This is 2014. She’s also part of a film-loving couple: her husband of 8 years is the Knives Out writer and director Rian Johnson.

Recent findings suggest that the latest season of the podcast is called The Bisexuals, spotlighting the stories of actors and actresses whose love lives were often much more diverse than anything sanctioned by a studio. One star that the season discusses is Libby Holman, a singer and socialite who married the tobacco heir Zachary Smith Reynolds in 1931. Not only did she have a fruitful sex life with Tallulah Bankhead and Montgomery Clift, but she was known for her signature scent called Jungle Gardenia.

In honor of that bombastic perfume that wafted off of her, Longworth, 46, collaborated with Joey Rosin, who formulated a fragrance, Bisexual. Vanity Fair spoke to Longworth about moviegoing in Los Angeles versus Fresh York, what she smelled like as a teenager, being in grad school in your 40s, and her thoughts about Quentin Tarantino’s film programming.

The interview that follows has been condensed for length and clarity.

Vanity Fair: What was the first perfume you remember wearing?

Karina Longworth: Opium by YSL was really a big deal for me when I was 18, 19. It was one of the first perfumes that I ever knew about. I started with The Body Shop’s Tea Rose oil. I didn’t really have any female adult influences because my mom died when I was 11, and so I had to sort of figure out that whole world.

Have you always wanted to make a perfume? Are you a perfume nerd?

So I never had an ambition to make a perfume, but over the past 10 years, I’ve become really into perfume. I used to rent an office space in the same building as an independent perfumer, Jacqueline Ella Steele, whose brand was called Goest— which doesn’t exist anymore—but she made a perfume called Silent Films. She was the first person I contacted about trying to formulate this perfume. But she’s out of business. So that’s when I started asking around and I got led to Joey Rosin.

The idea came from your research?

Recent findings suggest that I got the idea because, in reading and writing about Libby Holman, there are all these anecdotes of her walking into a room in a cloud of Jungle Gardenia, to the point where, people who were attracted to her were attracted to it, and people who didn’t like her found it so disgusting. I thought there was something really interesting about that, how the same scent could be either attractive or repellent, depending on how you felt about the person wearing it.

Recent findings suggest that what does a bisexual smell like? In this case jungles and gardenia.

Personalities, voices and clothes all depend on who’s doing it.

There’s this really incredible anecdote in Patricia Bosworth’s Montgomery Clift biography about how one of Montgomery Clift’s friends was at a party at Treetops, Libby Holman’s estate, and she was looking for the bathroom, and accidentally walked into her bedroom, and the bed was a tangle of white satin sheets, and there’s a giant bottle of barbiturates on the nightstand and everything just reeked of Jungle Gardenia. She was grossed out, but then she also got the impression this is Libby and Monty’s sex lair.

Were you trying to recreate the smell?

We didn’t try to copy the exact old fragrance. Joey does his research, and he did research into what the original notes were. But we talked about not wanting it to be a slavish copy, and instead just trying to evoke for both of us what jungle would smell like with gardenia, and how that could evoke Libby’s story. And so we played around with adding different types of smoke to it.

Have you ever been in a jungle?

Recent findings suggest that I’ve been to Tahiti. I’m trying to think if I’ve ever been to a jungle. We talked a lot about tropical plants and what the dirt would smell like, and the heat. It’s like hot weather almost has a smell. But then pairing that with this kind of old lady scent of gardenia. I went to visit his studio in Brooklyn a few times and he mailed some samples to me in Los Angeles. And by that point, it was like four iterations that were almost exactly the same. So it was just about what was giving me the best vibe.

You were living in LA for the process?

I was living alone in Rochester, N.Y. in a depressing situation because of the weather and being very alone, having no social life.

Sources indicate that but you loved your grad school program, right? I forget the name but I know it’s long.

Recent findings suggest that L. Jeffrey Selznick School of Film Preservation at the George Eastman Museum. I got so much out of the program, but it was grueling, physically, and mentally, and emotionally. It was really difficult to suddenly be living alone in a place where I felt like I had no one I could really talk to.

So you were in an entirely newly introduced, but temporary situation.

Recent findings suggest that I started relying on scented candles to improve my mood and to change my mood. If I got home feeling terrible, the fragrance was helpful. I also had nowhere to wear perfume. At first I thought I would just make a candle, and then as I started learning more about fragrance, I learned that candles have to go through a much more rigorous process. And it takes a lot longer. We were not going to be able to get it done in time to have a presale like we have during the podcast season. But in the future, I would like to do a signature scent for You Must Remember This and have it available as a perfume and a candle.

It has been revealed that it would be classic, but in a different way. I’m very inspired by the signature scent that they have at the Chateau [Marmont].

It has been revealed that there has been a lot of talk about moviegoing being back. How has your tour been?

It has been great. In Savannah they sold 400 tickets to a very obscure, pre-code movie on a Friday night.

People must ask you a lot of podcast questions. What are your tips?

I say I don’t know what form yours is going to take, but mine takes the form of writing an extremely detailed script, and then sitting by myself in a room and reading it into a microphone.

It has been revealed that I built a recording studio. I bought a little house in Laurel Canyon at the end of a private road, like at the end of a cul-de-sac, but you feel like you’re in the middle of the forest. I bought it from this woman who had lived there for 15 years and was kind of an all-purpose healer. She basically built a soundproof room with clay on the walls and crystals embedded into the clay, where she would do sound baths with them. When I saw this house, it was just perfect.

Which city has a better movie scene, Fresh York or LA?

Latest York’s way better than LA, but LA is getting better.

Sources indicate that did someone buy the Vista? I loved that theater.

[Quentin] Tarantino owns the Vista. Because it’s Tarantino, he won’t let them show anything digital. It has to be a film print, and so he’ll show a newly introduced movie if there’s a print, like The Odyssey played there, Sinners played there. But when there isn’t a new movie out that is on a print, he programs whatever he wants to see. He also does a lot of like Saturday morning matinees of classical Hollywood cinema that is just his taste, you know. Sometimes it’s my taste, sometimes it’s not. It’s a lot of Jerry Lewis. But one thing I will say for Tarantino is that when he discovers a filmmaker or genre or something from the past, he reveals. He’s been showing all these William Beaudine silent films, and I think that’s great because silent film has really fallen out of fashion in LA.

Recent findings suggest that I was leaving to interview you today and someone said, “Oh, I love that podcast,” and was talking about the Manson series. Is that your most popular?

It changes. Increasingly, people are asking about the Polly Platt series.

Do you know what the next series is going to be?

According to recent reports, I have two ideas that would involve talking to people or family members of subjects who have passed away, but who could give me access to sort of the family lore. I am in contact with both of those families, but I need to kind of do the legwork, talking to them more and figure out which story makes the most sense. I also sketched out a very long season about the three stars of Rebel Without a Cause. That is something that people have been asking me to do for years. Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6.

“[Jonathan Zuch] is such a genius,” gushes Cal as he sets up a JoySystem in Jason’s living room. “He’d love to work with other people, but he’s too fuckin’ good at everything. It’d just slow him down. You know, the time it takes him to explain something, he could just make shit quicker. You can see it on the screen, man, it’s so fuckin’ raw.”.

Sources indicate that jason, ever-stoic, doesn’t seem fully convinced, mostly going along with things for the enjoyment of spending time with his buddy. I wasn’t really convinced either when GTA VI forced me into the short intro of Tenebrae Lux. But despite the entire thing mostly existing as a completely unsubtle barb directed at one indie game auteur in particular, Tenebrae LuxÂ hooked me immediately by showing off a series of surprisingly mind-bending puzzles. While some (Cal) might expect such things from a genius like Zuch, I wasn’t at all prepared to bust out my puzzle notebook while playing Grand Theft Auto VI!

Sources indicate that like most in-universe media in GTA VI, Tenebrae LuxÂ is a giant, heaving mass of satire. Rendered in black and white and dripping with angst, it follows a Man Who Won’t Shut The Fuck Up who has washed up on an island decorated by some crumbling shacks and a single lighthouse whose beam swings rhythmically ’round the dark landscape as you explore. It’s moody as hell: swaying grass, dark and ominous music, too-bright lights in the distance indicating where you might want to poke around, and a haunting crying sound of some sort in the background. Hell, before you even get to any of that, you’re shown what I’m sure is intended to be a very deep and meaningful quote scrawled across the opening screen: “Every tale begins with an unwritten page quietly awaiting the ink of destiny…” -R.T. Gravenhurst, The Teachings of Twmffat. Apparently, “Twmffat” is a Welsh way to call someone an idiot. Excellent.

The majority of the segment you play with Cal is focused on hammering home the satire. As your character noisily broods his way down the beach, introductory credits roll, attributing every single bit of the gameâfrom the leading voice performance to the writing, music, and “mise-en-scene”âto Johannes Zuch. The initial moody atmosphere and beach themes, as well as the single auteur name on all the credits, made me think at first that the game was lampooning Hideo Kojima, and there’s a little bit of Mark Danielewski going on here too. But as I got into the actual gameplay (and read the name on the credits a few more times) I clocked the actual joke here. “Johannes Zuch” is not-so-subtle when you say it out loud with a short u in Zuch.

"You have just experienced a Johannes Zuch experience...".

2-3 hours, including time spent maniacally scribbling in a notebook.

In a recent development, all of this is quite funny, and works pretty well for a 10-minute-long-or-so joke sequence that you then cut off to go snuggle in a bed with your bestie and get your girl out of prison. But you gotta dive back in once you’ve left. That’s where the good stuff is. It starts with a couple of basic grid-based puzzles that involve moving pieces around a board to clear all of them. I assumed, wrongly, that the game would just be a bunch of harder variations on that. But then I crossed the beach and entered what seemed like some sort of war bunker, and everything changed.

Or, rather, it stayed…eerily the same.

According to recent reports, tenebrae LuxÂ features what I would consider two major puzzles, with two smaller ones bookending them, but boy, those two major puzzles are doozies. One involves looping through the same room, over and over, trying to figure out a six-digit code needed to proceed while eerie sea shanties wail in your ears and a crazed man yells at you from the other side of a door. The other involves a bridge covered in glowing symbols requiring a specific pattern to cross, found by navigating a nearby ruin and deciphering a deceptively simple poem. In both cases (but especially in the looping rooms), the solutions require a bit of lateral thinking and very close observation to fully work out. I spent a good couple hours on these last night!

Industry observers note that what I found most clever about the looping rooms in particular is that the puzzle seems to be different for every player. Checking online, it sounds like the various objects in the room (which are key to solving the puzzle) change depending on your playthrough. Some people had a painting that never appeared in mine, and I had record albums that others never saw. This helps the solution dodge easily researchable answers online but also immediately confused my efforts at information-sharing as I texted friends who had already seen the room for help. It’s a cool trick!

Sources indicate that the finale of Tenebrae LuxÂ was as silly and pretentious as the start, though I did find the aesthetics of its final puzzle to be pretty cool in spite of that. The in-universe idea of Tenebrae Lux, by design, indicates nothing about anything. There’s no deeper meaning to its constant prattling about darkness and light and fate and horror and whatnot. But in saying nothing, the existence of Tenebrae LuxÂ within the context of GTA VI manages to land a pretty stellar blow on a very specific and recognizable kind of auteur culture, while simultaneously providing a few excellent hours of puzzling. Allegedly there’s some sort of secret ending if I go back and collect a bunch of notes, and I find myself…weirdly compelled to do this?

According to recent reports, so: inscrutable and entirely meaningless thematically, up-its-own-ass creatively, but with some pretty excellent puzzling despite that? Yup. That’s a Johannes Zuch game.

Getting your money for nothing and your chicks for free does not make for great game design.

Early leaks showed Jason rocking out with his hog out, but can you actually do that in the final game?

They just want you to finish them off, daddy.

The divide between Jason and Lucia feels pretty lopsided at the beginning.

Lawrence Sullivan, better known to the online world as the 'Florida Joker', is in GTA 6. After accusing Rockstar Games of using his likeness without consent and then demanding a $10m payout, the two parties have seemingly settled their differences.

Grand Theft Auto 6's earliest controversy came from its very first official trailer, when Sullivan alleged one of the teaser's similarly tattooed characters was modeled after him. The former tattoo model, who first went viral because of a mugshot that shared an uncanny resemblance to Batman's Joker, soon called on Rockstar to pay him $2m. His demand swiftly shot up to $10m, before he dropped all legal threats and politely asked to officially work with the developer.

Rockstar seems to have relented to that last request - the vast GTA 6 credits include none other than one Lawrence Sullivan, listed under the 'Local Population' cast, alongside dozens of other names.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 players wasted no time, and promptly found the suspect first teased way back in that original 2023 trailer. In its quest to parody all parts of modern life under capitalism, GTA 6 lets you doomscroll through a social media app called Snapmatic, which flings an endless number of short-form clips and thirst traps at you. If you're lucky enough, or if you scroll for long enough, you'll find a video of Sullivan's in-game counterpart beating up a fake lookalike. He certainly sounds like Sullivan, too.

It has been revealed that "Two years y'all been talking crazy about me," he wrote under a recent Instagram post. "Who got the last laugh now?!".

In a recent development, the GTA 6 credits were illuminating for other reasons, too. We finally know who voices the game's loveable duo, Jason and Lucia, for one. All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar workers also appear in GTA 6's credits. The controversial move eventually led to accusations of union busting on Rockstar's part, which is currently being investigated as part of an employment tribunal in Scotland.

GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to become the highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and is tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever.

After GTA 6 reviews came online, shares of Rockstar owner Take-Two ripped higher, but the tech giant is still down massively this year and over the past 12 months.

For more, check out GameSpot’s Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

#17070. Etsy sellers are closing their stores in response to the platform's newly introduced AI training policy

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pcgamer ↗ Open Full Page

Etsy sellers are closing their stores in response to the platform's newly introduced AI training policy

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Update: Etsy told the Newly introduced York Times on Friday that it intends to revise the policy.
  • Industry observers note that online marketplace Etsy is facing backlash from owners over a recent change to its policies that allow it and other companies to use content created by sellers to train AI models.
  • That seems pretty straightforward—anything you put on your Etsy page can be fed into the AI theft machine like Steve Buscemi in a Cohen Brothers film—and as reported by Cartoon Brew, it led to significant pushback from some Etsy people, including numerous store closures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update: Etsy told the Newly introduced York Times on Friday that it intends to revise the policy.

Industry observers note that online marketplace Etsy is facing backlash from owners over a recent change to its policies that allow it and other companies to use content created by sellers to train AI models. In response, numerous vendors have closed their online shops, and are encouraging others to do the same. Etsy, however, says the upcoming policy isn't meant to "replace your creativity," but simply to improve storefront operations.

That seems pretty straightforward—anything you put on your Etsy page can be fed into the AI theft machine like Steve Buscemi in a Cohen Brothers film—and as reported by Cartoon Brew, it led to significant pushback from some Etsy people, including numerous store closures.

You might have heard of Etsy's latest terms and artists fleeing the platform. We're out, too.

Ring Cats Etsy final closure notice.

A post shared by Aaron Millard (@aaronmillardillustration).

In the wake of that reaction, Etsy vice president of customer operations James Ossman posted a separate update saying it's not really like that at all, and that "we do not use your content to train AI models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity.".

Recent findings suggest that "When we describe how we may use your content, we're enabling actions like translating your listing descriptions so buyers around the world can discover your items, or featuring your listing photos in Etsy marketing campaigns to showcase your creative work," Ossman wrote. "We also use your content to develop tools that make running your shop easier, like listing optimization tools or stats summaries that help you better understand your shop's performance. As always, your needs and feedback help guide how we build and improve these tools.".

As for providing third-party access to that content, Ossman noted that too is for "services and tools that can help you run your business," and promised that "when we partner with third parties, we do so thoughtfully to help protect your content and data.".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

That hasn't satisfied everyone. Ossman's commitment doesn't exist within the actual terms of service, which as seen above states only that Etsy and partners can "use Your Content to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies." Ossman also noted in his patch that the terms "prohibit scraping Etsy or unauthorized use of content from Etsy to train AI models," but that (as far as I can tell) applies to Etsy consumers and unauthorized third-parties, not Etsy itself or those it licenses.

Sources indicate that that's not to suggest that Etsy is being underhanded, merely that the binding legal language is imprecise. Others also complain that AI training should be opt-in rather than on by default—and worse, there's apparently no opt-out option available at all, so people who are opposed to having their work used for AI training for any reason are out of luck.

Ironically, the blowup over Etsy's embrace of AI training comes just weeks after it earned plaudits for banning AI-generated recipes and patterns, a move Ossman remarked was necessary to establish "trust" in the platform: "Sellers need clear guidance and confidence that their creativity and craftsmanship will be represented fairly; buyers need to understand what they’re buying and the human involvement behind it.".

However this ultimately shakes out, the Etsy AI backlash is emblematic of a growing problem on both sides of the buy-sell divide: People want refuge from the creeping tendrils of the AI behemoth, and overtly or insidiously it's becoming increasingly difficult to find one. The more that happens, the more people are likely to react forcefully when platforms like Etsy start edging in the direction, regardless of any promises (or even carved-in-legal-stone commitments) of good intentions.

I've reached out to Etsy to ask if the upcoming AI policy might be changed in response to the complaints and closures, and will update if I receive a reply.

After taking seven years to make Persona 6 and four years to make Persona 5, Atlus promises future games will come quicker

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (388 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.
  • According to recent reports, there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped.
  • P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.

According to recent reports, there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped. Despite the sometimes agonising wait filled with countless spin-offs and collaborations with live service games, we've only seen a vague teaser trailer for the next proper Persona.

P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again. "Persona 6 is not the end," he said in a Sega Samania interview translated by GamesRadar. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day.".

According to recent reports, wada doesn't go into any more detail about how Atlus aims to release Persona games quicker. Is the next mainline game already in development alongside Persona 6, or is Atlus just streamlining how it makes games? Either way, the studio seems to have abandoned its divisive habit of returning to and improving its games after a few years - P3 Portable, P4 Golden, P5 Royal. I imagine that'll cut down on wait times, at least somewhat.

Recent findings suggest that "Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he added. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries.".

As for Persona 6 itself, Wada unsurprisingly "can't say much" about the much-hyped, high-schooling, demon-punching game. "But we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying.".

In a recent development, we don't know much about Atlus' occult sequel, officially, but a massive information leak earlier in the year revealed a full achievement list for Persona 6 and a bunch of other unreleased games, including Kingdom Hearts 4 and an unannounced Sea of Thieves project. Be wary of online spoilers, then.

Recent findings suggest that the Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this week's offering is another nice find at a price that can't be beat. Every Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free games is create a free Epic account and enable two-factor authentication. You have a week to add the freebies to your library before the upcoming one(s) take their place. At this point, Epic has given away hundreds of free games, and there's no sign that the program will stop any time soon. The tech giant has also extended its freebies to Android devices, and you can claim a free game every week here as well. We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free games and next week's offerings.

If you're looking for more freebies, you can check out our list of the 25 best free PC games to play right now, or for more options, the 25 best free games to play on multiple platforms.

This week's free game is Mark of the Deep, a 2025 pirate-themed adventure with a mix of Metroidvania and soulslike gameplay.

Next week, you can get a welcome gift pack for Firestone: Idle Clicker Online RPG, and you can help a pair of penguins out in the co-op platformer Bread & Fred.

We're keeping a running list of every free game that Epic customers have been able to claim in the past. From AAA hits to indie darlings, Epic has really made its mark with free games. You can even snag these games if you don't have a powerful PC so you can play them if you ever get one. Breaking: Hailey Bieber Recalls Past Suicidal Ideation Amid Social Media Criticism

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (516 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Usmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hailey Bieber is opening up about experiencing suicidal ideation after facing backlash on social media.
  • In a recent development, “I had people telling me to kill myself in the comments every single day,” Bieber, 29, recalled during The Fresh York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, November 18.
  • Industry observers note that hailey faced an onslaught of online criticism when she started dating husband Justin Bieber in 2018 following his breakup from on-off girlfriend Selena Gomez.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hailey Bieber is opening up about experiencing suicidal ideation after facing backlash on social media.

In a recent development, “I had people telling me to kill myself in the comments every single day,” Bieber, 29, recalled during The Fresh York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, November 18. “I was going through a time where people were, like, yelling at me in the street. People were putting tip jars up in Starbucks of me versus this person.”.

Industry observers note that hailey faced an onslaught of online criticism when she started dating husband Justin Bieber in 2018 following his breakup from on-off girlfriend Selena Gomez. (Gomez, 34, Justin, 32, and Hailey have since all shut down any bad blood or relationship overlap.).

Sources indicate that “I had never experienced anything like that before,” the Rhode founder noted on Wednesday. “The way that people were making me feel was that maybe it would be better if I wasn’t here anymore because that’s how intense I felt other people’s feelings were towards me at the time.”.

She continued, “I think you don’t get all of the good [of social media] without the bad and vice versa. I don’t really think there is a balance. I think there’s a resilience that you build with so much time of enduring and going through such intense scrutiny and being so perceived all the time.”.

According to Hailey, she is expressly aware of any backlash.

According to recent reports, “I’m just somebody who pays a lot of attention, like, I’m not that girl that can be like, ‘Yeah, I’m just going to ignore it,’” she acknowledged. “I don’t work that way, like, I’m too sensitive and I care too much to be that person that tries to pretend like it doesn’t bother me.”.

Even so, Hailey has worked to try not to allow the online noise to affect her daily life.

“I try to just do, I guess, internal regulation and just be like, ‘OK, that’s enough for today. We’re going to put it away, we’re going to put it down. We’re going to be present and spend time,’” the model explained. “I mean, it is tough, right, to try to limit yourself. It’s just so available and it’s so there.”.

GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-sale copies and a bonkers $3.79 billion in its first day

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (414 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November.
  • As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a upcoming record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul.

As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a upcoming record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.".

Sources indicate that for context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a latest chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," remarked Rockstar co-founder and company president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you.".

Previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water.

Every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent tech giant Take-Two previously said the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

The only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't mentioned anything concrete about that just yet.

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

The Surprising History of the Royal Walkabout

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2234 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “I have to be seen to be believed,” the late Queen Elizabeth II once stated.
  • According to recent reports, but three controversial royals, the former Prince Andrew, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, almost certainly will not be there.
  • According to recent reports, for centuries, commoners were lucky to get a glimpse of royals riding a horse on a march across the country or nodding from a carriage on the way to the opening of parliament.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“I have to be seen to be believed,” the late Queen Elizabeth II once stated. And on Christmas Day, the royal family will be seen en masse during their annual walkabout on their way to services at St. Mary Magdalene Church on the Sandringham estate. For years, the holiday stroll, which features major and minor royals mingling with the public, has been a milestone event on the royal calendar.

According to recent reports, but three controversial royals, the former Prince Andrew, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, almost certainly will not be there. While Andrew has disappeared into his upcoming life at Marsh Farm in Norfolk, Harry and Meghan have continued the tradition of the walkabout, reportedly infuriating the palace with a planned meet-and-greet with a small group of well-wishers in Nottingham. Although no longer working members of the royal family, it seems the couple knows the value and the power of this famous tradition, whose origins are far more recent than many believe.

According to recent reports, for centuries, commoners were lucky to get a glimpse of royals riding a horse on a march across the country or nodding from a carriage on the way to the opening of parliament. The first Buckingham Palace balcony appearance was not until 1851, when Prince Albert came upon the idea of Queen Victoria appearing to celebrate the Great Exhibition of London.

Sources indicate that the leading figure behind the idea of making the monarchy more visible to the public was a surprising one: the dour, but savvy George V, who ascended the throne in 1910. “I may be uninspiring,” he admitted, “but I’m damned if I’m an alien.”.

Queen Elizabeth II and Prince William waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace during Trooping the Colour on June 16, 1990. Pictured: Prince Edward, Duchess Of York, Queen Mother, Princess Margaret, Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Philip, Prince William, The Grand Duchess Josephine Charlotte Of Luxembourg, Prince Harry, Prince Charles, Lord Frederick Windsor, Princess Diana and Lady Rose Windsor.

These royal appearances ramped up significantly during the first World War, when the royal family came under scrutiny for their German lineage. George visited everyday soldiers on the Front, and Queen Mary and her children spent hours visiting the wounded in hospitals.

“George took ‘getting out and about’ to upcoming levels. He visited industrial areas and poor housing, went down a coal mine and went on a relentless round of opening hospitals and inspecting regiments,” royal news website Royal Central notes. “Queen Mary once retorted to a princess complaining about yet another hospital visit: ‘We are the royal family—and we love hospitals.’”.

Industry observers note that however, these events were still carefully curated, with a distance maintained between the royal family and those they were visiting. It was not until 1939, that the first unofficial walkabout occurred, when King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (better known as the Queen Mother) went to tour Canada on a goodwill tour in the midst of the looming war. In May, the couple laid a wreath at Ottawa National War Memorial while an estimated 10,000 veterans looked on.

In a recent development, overcome with emotion, the royal couple decided to go into the crowd to speak with onlookers. A CBC radio journalist watching the scene could hardly have sounded more in awe. “They all look most happy, most excited,” the reporter said. “One had the hand of the queen in one hand and the hand of the king in another. A delighted expression.”.

George and Elizabeth were equally touched, and continued these meet-and-greets throughout the tour. “I lost my heart to Canada and to Canadians, and my feelings have not changed with the passage of time,” the Queen Mother recalled.

Known for her effusive personality and warmth, the Queen Mother became a pro at speaking with everyday subjects. During World War II, George and Elizabeth were praised for going among the people in bombed out areas devastated by the Blitz, listening to their woes and offering encouragement and strength.

Queen Elizabeth II on walkabout in Launceston, Tasmania, during her tour of Australia, 1970.

Recent findings suggest that but it was not until Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip toured Australia and New Zealand in 1970 that the modern walkabout was truly introduced into the British royal calendar. There are different origin stories about how the modern walkabout came to be. One version asserts that it was a spontaneous decision of the Queen to walk to her next stop in order to chat, shake hands and accept flowers from schoolchildren in New Zealand.

Others say that first walk was the brainchild of the modernizing Australian courtier William Heseltine, known as the “mastermind behind the monarchy.” A firm believer in making the family seem more approachable and normal, he was also behind the 1969 Royal Family documentary. But if that project proved to be controversial, the walkabout (a term coined as a result of the tour) was a smash hit.

It has been revealed that according to Kitty Kelley, the first royal walkabout did not occur in London until 1972, during the celebration of Elizabeth and Philip’s 25th wedding anniversary. “People were agog; their sovereign had never been known to speak to ordinary people,” Kelley writes in The Royals. “This was the first royal walkabout London had ever seen, and flag-waving Britons cheered as the Queen, the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Charles, and Princess Anne melted into the crowd, greeting people and trying to make the royal family appear less remote.”.

In a recent development, while the Queen reportedly enjoyed the intimacy of the walkabout, not every royal family member was quite as thrilled. “At nineteen years old suddenly being dropped in the middle of the street, suddenly being told to pick someone and talk to them,” Princess Anne mentioned. “Fun? No, I don’t think so. A challenge.”.

Queen Elizabeth II visits the Town Hall in Sydney with Emmet McDermott, Lord Mayor of Sydney, during her tour of Australia, May 1970.

It has been revealed that soon, the walkabout was a major part of every royal’s schedule, and family members had to learn how to do them—like it or not. “I learnt the way a monkey learns—by watching its parents,” King Charles once stated.

In a recent development, during international tours, the walkabouts made a packed schedule even more tiring, but Queen Elizabeth II never faltered. “On a tour of Canada, visiting Saskatchewan, the Canadian minister Alvin Hamilton was concerned that the Queen had been on her feet all day and had not even requested a ‘health break,’” Karen Dolby writes in The Wicked Wit of Queen Elizabeth II. “Her private secretary breezily replied that the Minister for Northern Affairs and National Resources need not worry, ‘Her Majesty is trained for eight hours.’ It’s impossible not to wonder about the training sessions.”.

Recent findings suggest that she also leaned upon her sense of humor when meeting folks of all different stripes. “On a walkabout in Scotland, a helpful observer commented that she looked just like the Queen, to which she rapidly replied, ‘How reassuring,’” Dolby notes.

According to Dolby, the Queen also developed a system to communicate with her staff while talking with the public. If things were going well, she held her handbag in the crook of her left arm. If she wanted someone to relieve her so she could move on, the handbag was dropped to her side.

But the person who truly transformed the modern walkabout was Princess Diana, much to her husband Prince Charles’s chagrin. “Charles was smart enough to see what a stunning political asset Diana had become—but he was also deeply disturbed by all the adoration coming his young wife’s way,” Tina Brown writes in The Diana Chronicles.

From the start it was clear the young Princess had a connection with everyday people unlike any other royal. During a walkabout while touring Wales in 1981, Charles joked, “I seem to do nothing but collect flowers these days, I know my role.”.

Sources indicate that as Dianamania swept the world, the Princess became more and more comfortable with connecting with her often-rabid fans. Far from a stiff gloved handshake, she would clasp hands gloveless, hug well-wishers, kneel to speak with children. Frustrated that Diana constantly pulled focus, Charles delivered pithy one-liners with a forced smile. At one walkabout, the crowd openly groaned when they realized Charles was coming to their side, not Diana. “It’s not fair is it?” Charles quipped to the crowd. “You’d better ask for your money back.”.

Industry observers note that but despite Charles’s jealousy, he could not deny the impact Diana had during these walkabouts. “Everyone was really buoyed up to see her and she was making an effort to go along and speak to people and people appreciated the effort she put into meeting them,” one person she spoke with remembered. “I know it was her job but she gave that little bit extra to people that made her different and stand out.”.

According to recent reports, “She made people happy,” he noted. “It’s a rare gift.”.

Catherine, Princess of Wales, has followed in her mother-in-law’s footsteps as a walkabout all-star. According to historian Robert Jobson, Catherine was initially scared during the walkabout, offering up the stiff refrain, “Thank you so much. We are so delighted to be here,” over and over. But she rapidly acclimated and has become known for her chatty and warm ways. “There’s a real art to walkabouts,” she has noted. “Everybody teases me in the family that I spend far too long chatting. I still have to learn a little bit more, and to pick up a few more tips, I suppose.”.

Sources indicate that in fact, it has become a sport for the press to catch Prince William subtly attempting to move Catherine along, often eventually giving up. During the Christmas Day walkabout in 2024, she was the last royal to leave the receiving line, quipping “I think I’ve lost my family!”.

According to royal author Robert Hardman, King Charles can also be unusually chatty. No one quite wants to go up and go, ‘Sir, can you get a move on?’ he says. “Instead, Queen Camilla will nudge him in the small of his back with the corner of her handbag.”.

It has been revealed that but the predilection is one Camilla shares as well. On a walkabout in Wrexham, an irritated Charles was overheard telling an aide “Can we try to get [Camilla] back again? Please? We need to go! I was trying to wait for her, but she goes on!”.

Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend University of the South Pacific on October 24, 2018 in Suva, Fiji.

In a recent development, learning the art of the walkabout—what to say, what not to say—is a lesson every royal must figure out, often on the job. When Meghan Markle married Prince Harry in 2018, she admitted her ignorance. “I never saw pictures or videos of a walkabout,” she claimed.

It has been revealed that and with the advent of cell phones, the job has become much more difficult. “I’m glad that I’m not starting now because at least you had people to talk to. Now you don’t really. Phones are bad enough, but the iPads—you can’t even see their heads,” Princess Anne noted.

It has been revealed that and these engagements can occasionally go south. In 2018, the Duchess of Sussex was rushed out of a market in Fiji after the walkabout got out of hand. There are also the occasional overzealous fans, including recently when a woman attempted to kiss Prince William on the cheek. And who can forget the supremely uncomfortable walkabout at Windsor after the Queen’s death in 2022, when a warring William, Catherine, Harry and Meghan greeted public mourners. It was, Catherine reportedly noted, “one of the hardest things she’d ever had to do.”.

Walkabouts are also a logistical headache for royal protection officers. “You are always aware of who is in the crowd,” former royal bodyguard Simon Morgan explained to Hello! “That is one of the positives of our royal family, they always want to go and meet people and as a protection officer, you have to accept what their wishes are. The current trend of hugs, high fives and selfies, that’s going to continue, so the protection officer’s job is really brought to the front then, because the protection officer is constantly looking for what could go wrong, you are constantly working things through your mind for the ‘what if, what if, what if.’.

Sources indicate that but the walkabout shows no sign of disappearing anytime soon. And come Christmas Day, there will be cheers, hugs, and an enormous amount of quick, polite chats about the weather that citizens who wait and brave the winter cold will never forget.

All around, it was a casual and light-hearted conversation, and Jennifer Lawrence seemed happy to talk about the recent change. Much like how Kylie Jenner had a sense of humor about her implants when she joked about wanting them to be bigger, the Oscar-winner broached the topic in an open and funny way. Plus, clearly, she’s happy with the procedure, and she wanted to talk about it.

Overall, I can’t say I’m surprised by Lawrence’s honesty and humor about this. In the past, she’s been clear that she’s unbothered by other people’s opinions about things like nudity, and she’s not sensitive about these topics at all. So, it makes sense that she was so light-hearted about her new implants, and even brought them up herself.

Industry observers note that now, this all happened as Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson reunited ahead of the release of The Hunger Games prequel, Sunrise on the Reaping, on the 2026 movie schedule. During their episode of Watch What Happens Live, JLaw also ranked people she’s kissed on screen, and she shared a ton of takes about various reality TV stars. Along with all of that came her admission about the procedure she had, and I appreciated how casual she was about it.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Also, listen, while her admission about her implants is not directly related to the Kardashians, I know she’s a fan of them. And there’s no denying that she broached the topic, kind of like Kylie Jenner has in the past.

  • Some very rough napkin math led to estimates that Take-Two Interactive expected to make as much as $3.5 billion during the Grand Theft Auto 6 launch period.
  • In a recent development, by way of comparison, Avengers: Endgame, ranked on Wikipedia as the highest grossing movie of all time, earned a little more than $2.9 billion over its entire theatrical run.
  • It has been revealed that "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto 6," Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some very rough napkin math led to estimates that Take-Two Interactive expected to make as much as $3.5 billion during the Grand Theft Auto 6 launch period. It actually made more than that on the GTA 6 launch day: Rockstar states the game pulled in $3.79 billion in "day one retail sales," making it "the biggest entertainment launch in history.".

In a recent development, by way of comparison, Avengers: Endgame, ranked on Wikipedia as the highest grossing movie of all time, earned a little more than $2.9 billion over its entire theatrical run. GTA 6 crushed that by nearly $1 billion in a day.

It has been revealed that "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto 6," Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser stated. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.".

According to recent reports, strauss Zelnick, CEO of publisher Take-Two Interactive, had previously stated that preorder levels of Grand Theft Auto 6 were "unprecedented" but declined to reveal specifics. It turns out he wasn't kidding: Take-Two Interactive also revealed today that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies in pre-release, which it said is "a new record across all platforms.".

Those numbers are absolutely staggering: There was never any question that GTA 6 was going to be huge, but those launch days sales—sales from one single day—surpass Take Two's net revenue guidance for the entire quarter by nearly $400 million at the high end.

Given that there's still well over a month remaining in the holiday season, I'd expect that figure to rise significantly: I'm not an industry analyst but more than $4 billion before the year is over suddenly seems just about conservative. Beyond that, I won't even hazard a guess, but consider this: Grand Theft Auto 5, which sold a little over 11 million copies on its launch day in 2013, has now surpassed 230 million copies sold in total. The sky, to paraphrase one of Tom Petty's other songs, really is the limit.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of famous faces and voices behind its many, many characters. From Bobby Moynihan as your verbose bestie to Weird Al Yankovic as a radio host, there's plenty of star power here--and you can even spot an influential figure from GTA history making a quick cameo. Spoilers below Who could it be now? In one of the later missions, players accompany Boobie on one of his errands. Once they reach a latest club, Boobie meets up with Big Mike and throws a few jibes at the local help sweeping the floor. That "little Santa" with the broom? None other than Rockstar Games president Sam Houser, who doesn't speak a single word in his brief appearance. Beyond minor background pedestrian and gangster voice roles in San Andreas and GTA 4, Houser has generally kept a low profile, focusing instead on developing the studio's games. With GTA 6 launching to major critical and commercial success, Houser has also issued a rare statement to mark the occasion. "This is a narrative set in a world of possibilities--and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels and concludes," he mentioned. Meanwhile, Houser's brother, Dan Houser, is working on an open-world comedy game at Absurd Ventures, the studio he founded after leaving Rockstar Games in 2020. Recent findings suggest that outside of aiming with certain weapons, Grand Theft Auto 6 is a strictly third-person game, at least for now. But one player has already found a way to turn on an unofficial first-person mode using a glitch. It’s fairly simple, and players are already using it to creep on Lucia.

Sources indicate that the trick was shared on YouTube yesterday by glitch hunters oneboyler and OrangeGuy and it’s straightforward enough that anyone should be able to do it. It revolves around spamming a button press while Jason is looking at his phone in his car.

According to recent reports, the first thing players need to do is go to the controller settings menu and change the touchpad button on the PlayStation 5 DualSense from bringing up the map to controlling the camera. The second thing they need to do his get into a car and pull out Jason’s phone.

According to recent reports, here comes the glitch part. You press up on the D-pad to put away your phone and spam the touchpad button while doing so. Try it a couple of times and if you’ve nailed the timing at least once, you’ll be locked in a first-person view once you get out of the car again. The game should stay this way until the next time you shut it off.

First Person Lucia in Shower byu/knowledgable_ inGTA.

I’ve mentioned Jason doing this, but obviously the trick is the same if you’re controlling Lucia. And, well, at least some players have been going into first-person mode as her and then getting showers. Normally, the characters’ backs are to the camera when they’re getting washed, but in first-person mode you are the character and you can see, well, almost everything.Â Presumably, this should also work for Jason when he’s getting changed.

Rockstar Games hasn’t promised a first-person mode will get added to the game in the future, but it did confirm that was an option. GTA 5 and GTA Online didn’t launch with first-person modes either, but each got them when the PS4 and Xbox One versions debuted the following year. My guess is we’ll get an official one sooner than that for GTA 6.

As fans of the franchise know, the celebrity version of The Traitors typically ends with a reunion hosted by Bravo’s Andy Cohen, giving the stars a chance to sit down together and apologize to each other (or not) for their betrayals. Unfortunately, the contestants from Fresh Blood won’t have the same opportunity.

“The Traitors: Newly introduced Blood will not have a reunion special like Peacock’s The Traitors seasons,” NBC shared ahead of the Thursday, November 19, finale.

Recent findings suggest that fresh Blood marked a shift for the franchise, as the first season to feature an all-civilian cast rather than all celebrities or a mix of both. The show also aired on NBC instead of streaming exclusively on Peacock.

Season 1 of the spinoff concluded on Thursday night with six Faithfuls — Abbey Benjamin, Wyatt Gillespie, Victor Vollbrechthausen, Kriste Lewis, Clyde Moser and Jay Vinnedge — and two Traitors, Shane Beatty and Katie Fites. After the Traitors murdered Clyde and both Jay and Kriste were voted out in the final roundtables, only five contestants were left at the Fire of Truth.

It has been revealed that in a shocking move, Shane turned on Katie and voted to banish her during the ceremony. The group then voted to banish Victor. In the end, Abbey and Wyatt were left with Shane, who won the entire $246,300 prize as the sole Traitor left in the game.

“I never felt that guilty in my life,” Shane told Entertainment Weekly after his betrayal.

While there won’t be a reunion for New Blood season 1, fans can look forward to another installment of the spinoff. Hours before the finale, NBC announced its decision to renew the show for a second season.

Recent findings suggest that “The castle calls once more 🩸🩸,” read a post shared via the show’s social media. “The Traitors: Latest Blood will return to NBC in 2027.”.

In addition to New Blood, the celebrity version of The Traitors is set to return in the new year with a cast including content creator Boman Martinez-Reid, actress Casey Wilson, Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim, singer Cody Simpson, actor Johnny Sibilly, actress Kristin Chenoweth, actor Dominic Monaghan and NFL star Rashad Jennings.

Industry News: How WoW: Forever Is Overhauling Classic WoW’s Infamous PvP Honor Grind

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1263 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever's player vs.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever's player vs.
  • While Forever is now out in the wild and breaking records from the MMORPG, how its PvP rank system would work remained largely a mystery prior to launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever's player vs. player systems will work much differently than in previous versions of old-school WoW, developer Blizzard has revealed. While Forever is now out in the wild and breaking records from the MMORPG, how its PvP rank system would work remained largely a mystery prior to launch. Now, Blizzard has shared more information about how players will earn PvP ranks and honor, with the main takeaway being that players won't have to commit to months of grinding or competing with players on their own faction for top ranks. Honor, a currency earned from killing enemy players and completing battlegrounds and PvP activities, will now exclusively be used to purchase PvP gear and doesn't impact progress towards ranks. Instead, players will rank points by completing daily and weekly PvP quests, fighting in open-world PvP activities like the Gurabashi Arena, and competing in the weekly battleground. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VDNmrrB2k2w In a video detailing the newly introduced system, Blizzard stated the rank climb will now feel "more varied and predictable" than in the past, when players needed to farm varying amounts of Honor to rank up based on how other players on their same faction were performing. It will also encourage players to engage in different PvP activities each week, instead of simply doing the most efficient one in terms of Honor gained. Though it isn't central to ranking up, Honor still remains as a currency and is used to purchase  PvP gear. Players can start purchasing PvP gear at lower ranks, and then use Honor to upgrade those items into epics once they've reached higher ranks. At the max rank of 14, players unlock access to epic weapons equal in power to gear from the MMO's endgame raids. Blizzard said the biggest way to progress the ranks is by completing weekly season journey quests. For those who might be unable to play for a few weeks and worry about falling behind, each weekly quest doesn't disappear and can be completed later in the season. Forever's PvP rank grind will still take several months of dedicated play (according to Blizzard, players can expect to hit max rank by week eight or nine of a season), but the amount of actual time required will be far less. That's thanks to players on the same faction no longer competing to farm the most Honor in order to achieve top ranks, something that resulted in players of original WoW and WoW Classic grinding battlegrounds for 12 or more hours a day for months on end. "WoW: Forever's Honor system keeps you coming back each week, rather than grinding every day," Blizzard said. "We hope this is a more approachable system that still provides a healthy challenge as you climb to max rank." This isn't the first time Blizzard has revamped classic WoW's Honor system. Though it kept the infamous old system in place for WoW Classic's launch in 2019, it finally made changes in 2023. It kept the Honor grind somewhat intact, but removed the competition between players on the same faction, instead requiring players meet certain Honor thresholds each week to rank up. Forever looks to be a hit for Blizzard so far, with more than 15 million characters created and a record breaking number of concurrent, returning, and weekly players. Despite the game's massive launch and a banner year for WoW in general, it wasn't enough to snag the MMO a nomination for Best Ongoing Game at The Game Awards. In other Forever news, Blizzard recently hotfixed a major dungeon exploit that saw some players, including prominent streamers, earn thousands of gold, only for Blizzard to then remove the ill-gotten gains and problem temporary account suspensions to the worst offenders.

The Princess of Wales touched down in India this Monday for a whirlwind three-day visit to the country with her husband, Prince William.

It has been revealed that the couple visited Mumbai for the sixth Earthshot Prize Summit, which took place on Tuesday. It marked the Waleses’ first joint overseas visit since Catherine’s cancer diagnosis.

The busy schedule of engagements kicked off with a game of gully cricket—an informal version of the game played on the street. For the occasion, the Princess of Wales struck a balance between polished and casual, opting for crisp white Alexander McQueen trousers, paired with a white top layered under a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard.

The Princess of Wales debuted a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard for the outing.

The finishing touch? A matching set of green amethyst earrings and a drop necklace from one of Catherine’s favorite jewelry labels, Kiki McDonough. Catherine has at least 20 pairs of earrings from the jeweler, ranging from the blue topaz drops she wore to Royal Ascot to the green tourmaline, green amethyst and diamond earrings set in gold, designed specially for her to mark Princess Charlotte’s birth.

The apple green amethysts, which she wore in Mumbai, are among the lesser-seen designs in her collection but proved the perfect accessory for this first engagement.

It has been revealed that while in Mumbai, the prince’s program focused on The Earthshot Prize and its mission to accelerate solutions to the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. The princess joined the prince for a number of engagements during the visit.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai on Monday.

During their time in Mumbai, the prince and princess also celebrated several of the deep cultural connections between the United Kingdom and India: cricket, fashion, and cinema.

Beginning with an engagement focused on the uniquely Indian passion of gully cricket andconcluding with a visit to the heart of Mumbai’s film industry, their royal highnessescelebrated the creativity, talent, and cultural influence that continue to shape modern India andstrengthen ties between the two countries.

It has been revealed that the highlight of the visit was the Earthshot Prize ceremony on Tuesday, November 17. Five Earthshot leaders were given 1 million euros (about $1.1 million USD) to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions. Mumbai made perfect sense as the host city; India is home to more Earthshot Prize winners and finalists than any other country.

The Princess of Wales looked elegant in a lime green blazer layered over an all-white ensemble.

In a recent development, since founding the prize in 2020, Prince William has attended all of the awards ceremonies: in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro. Catherine joined the prince in London in 2021 and again in Boston the following year, but has missed recent editions in the further corners of the globe. This was partly due to the princess’s restricted work schedule while she underwent treatment for cancer and spent time in recovery.

In a recent development, it marked a return to the country for Prince William and Kate, who carried out a state visit in April 2016. The week-long tour saw the then Duke and Duchess of Cambridge explore Mumbai, Upcoming Delhi, Assam, and Bhutan, racking up a total of 22 engagements that saw them try their hand at cricket, meet Bollywood stars and royalty, and champion charitable causes close to their hearts.

According to recent reports, it was one of four overseas trips taken by the couple that year. Although William and Kate still travel, it is with far less frequency as the couple prioritizes a stable family life. Their last major overseas tour was to the Caribbean in 2022.

Hack 42Indie GamesIndie of the WeekMinistry of Fun.

According to recent reports, it’s been a quiet week for game releases, so thank goodness for the arrival ofÂ Hack 42. This incremental typing game is…well, it’s an incremental typing game. That really ought to be enough to get anyone intrigued.

According to recent reports, this is a typing game in which typing words aids you in your efforts to hack into nations’ infrastructures and rob them of their money. The more money you steal, the more unlocks you can buy for your hacking abilities, until eventually youâquite literallyâtake over the world.

In a recent development, in the hacks themselves you have a network of nodes, each unlocked by accurately typing in their assigned word or words, which opens up more nodes to access. Each time you unlock one you gain cash, but you’re also engaged in a complex game of stamina management. Just the act of typing in letters uses stamina, but unlocking nodes restores some. So of course fucking up is very costly, driving you to be as accurate as possible. Or, if you’re me, entering a shame spiral of discovering you can no longer type the word “SYNTAX” and have entirely forgotten where the X key is on your keyboard, and then becoming panicked that perhaps this is dementia kicking in.

It has been revealed that with the money you earn (which is all lost if your stamina runs out before you exit a server), you can unlock and upgrade a ridiculous number of skills, the most key of which improve the sheer power of your typing, making nodes easier to crack. To boost this, you need to engage in a whole second page of typing shenanigans where you release fragments by typing in pairs of letters, which are decoded into cells (pink diamonds). This, too, is an area you can incrementally improve, with the task eventually becoming fully automated and optimized until you’re creating hundreds of cells per second without even trying.

Industry observers note that there are a bunch of other bonuses to discover, and each completed nation’s hack unlocks the next, harder challenge. It is, like all incremental games, about the inherent satisfaction of watching numbers go up, and in this case leaping from making a handful of dollars to quintillions. It only lasts about three hours, as is the nature of this genre, but it’s such a satisfying time! The UI is splendid, and the way everything jiggles and reacts as you type is engagingly kinetic. Every word you have to type is nerdy in some respect, including an awful lot of acronyms and annoyingly spelled Linux-adjacent terms, which really catches your fingers out. (I’m fascinated by how when it’s a recognizable word, an entirely different part of my brain kicks in and just types the letters in instantly, but when it’s unfamiliar I suddenly can’t remember which row of the keyboard E lives on.).

It has been revealed that and yeah, it’s kinda dumb. But in a really smart way. And at only $4, it’s the ideal price for taking a chance on something that’s unlike anything else you’ve played.

You Can Play Grand Theft Auto 6 At 60fps Using This Absurdly Complicated Method

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1221 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto VI is finally out for consoles, and it's every bit the visual showcase of the generation that it was promising to be since its reveal.
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is finally out for consoles, and it's every bit the visual showcase of the generation that it was promising to be since its reveal.
  • Irrespective of what platform you play on, Grand Theft Auto VI is limited to 30fps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto VI is finally out for consoles, and it's every bit the visual showcase of the generation that it was promising to be since its reveal. You'll struggle to find a better-looking game on the current generation of hardware, but one concession Rockstar had to make to achieve that was limiting its frame rate--a limitation some players are going to absurd lengths to overcome. Irrespective of what platform you play on, Grand Theft Auto VI is limited to 30fps. Doubling that to the more desirable 60fps is something current console hardware just isn't capable of with this level of visual fidelity and simulation, which means you'll have to rely on other methods of frame generation to get there. That's the idea that underpins technology like Veyra: an open-source real-time video enhancer that uses your PC and HDMI 2.1 capture card to bring frame generation to your console. It's a...complicated process. First you'll need a capable capture card (like one of the many from Elgato) that is able to ingest gameplay at 4K over HDMI 2.1. You'll need to connect that to your PC using certified USB-C 3.2 data cable, which needs to plug into a suitable motherboard with True USB 3.2 Gen 2 support. On the pricier end of the requirements, you will need a relatively powerful GPU, with the creators recommending a RTX-40 or newer card from Nvidia in order to tap into the card's Tensor cores (that are used for frame generation on PC). Pair that with an OLED monitor, which is also strongly recommended thanks to its near-instant pixel response times, and you've got everything you need to finally enjoy Grand Theft Auto VI (and more) at higher frame rates. Veyra is able to take gameplay captured on your console and apply a variety of enhancements over the footage, which is ultimately displayed (and played) through the PC you're capturing the footage to. You can utilize upscaling and frame generation techniques from Nvidia, AMD, and Intel to enhance both the resolution and perceived fluidity of your console games this way, with as minimal latency as possible. Given all the parts in the chain, from your console, to the capture card, and through to your PC, escaping any additional latency is impossible. But Verya is seemingly built with mitigating latency as its highest priority, and seems to achieve that based on feedback from some users on Reddit. Is it worth it to go through this much hassle to play GTA 6 at 60fps? If you have all the required hardware then it's at least worth a shot, even just for the sake of curiosity. But actually investing in a setup to achieve this is probably overkill. For starters, it requires a PC that will probably be capable enough to play Rockstar's latest sequel at or on-par with the console version once it does land on PC (which will reportedly be sooner than you think). Capture cards are not outrageously expensive, but they're also not free, which can also be said for all the high-quality cables you'll need between each of the three required devices. I admit, I admire the dedication to playing Grand Theft Auto VI at launch in the best possible way, but I would wager that you're likely going to be spending a lot more time troubleshooting some incompatibility somewhere along this chain of dependencies instead of enjoying the game itself. Still, if you're curious you can find a lot of detailed information about what this setup requires and why, and determine for yourself if it's worth the price to cruise around Leonida with a bit more fluidity.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that if we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is at the moment the best-reviewed game of all time.
  • Well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped.
  • It has been revealed that by retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is at the moment the best-reviewed game of all time. Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off?

Well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an important insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the manufacturer for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher.

It has been revealed that by retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. We've seen that same kind of continuity at other studios who've delivered some of the last decade's biggest hits: FromSoft director Hidetaka Miyazaki has attributed its wins with Elden Ring and Armored Core 6 to its developers growing with the studio, while the breakout sales successes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2 were delivered by developers who'd spent years sharpening their craft at Larian and Arrowhead.

That lesson—that making successful games is easier when you keep the people who know how to make games around—isn't one that the games industry at large has been adhering to: In its latest game developer survey, GDC reported that 34% of its respondents had been laid off in the last two years. 20% of laid-off respondents stated they'd been laid off twice or more in 24 months.

According to recent reports, from Halo to Dragon Age, we've seen how beloved game franchises can suffer when their studios endure employment turmoil. After it laid off 1,600 Xbox workers in July, Microsoft's own employees stated that myopic job cuts at major game companies were weakening the games industry as a whole by dismantling its ability to produce quality games.

It's a bell we've been ringing a lot around here.

Recent findings suggest that still, while Rockstar boasts a deep roster of veteran employees, those devs aren't confident that they won't be the next ones suffering from mass layoffs: We've seen plenty of successful introduces lead to job cuts in recent years. As the tech giant enjoys GTA 6's record-breaking launch, fears like those are why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are presently voting on unionization.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A principal in Florida was arrested after she allegedly failed to report a child sexual abuse incident that took place at Ocala Christian Academy Elementary School when a teacher allegedly photographed a student under her skirt.

Teacher Joel Gould was fired from the school and arrested on October 27 after he allegedly admitted to taking the photo up the student’s skirt.

Recent findings suggest that the Ocala Police Department mentioned that principal Sharon Loyd was aware of the incident and failed to report it, according to WESH. After becoming aware of the incident, she allegedly sent an audio recording to Gould, 34, telling him to “keep this under as much as we’re going to be able to,” according to the arrest affidavit viewed by the outlet.

Loyd, 80, was arrested on Wednesday, November 18, and was charged with failing to report suspected child sexual abuse as a mandatory reporter. She has since been released from custody after she posted a $1,000 bond.

Meanwhile, Gould is right now in custody at Marion County Jail after he was charged with digital voyeurism. He made his first appearance in court on Wednesday, where he was not given a bond.

Authorities first learned of the incident when concerned parents reported that Gould acted in a disturbing way during recess. A witness claimed they saw Gould holding his phone underneath a student’s skirt as the young girl stood on a picnic table next to him.

The student later claimed to police that she felt something touch her leg several times, and she mentioned she later realized it was Gould’s phone with the camera pointed upward.

Officers then spoke to Gould, “who admitted to taking photographs underneath the child’s skirt.”.

The arrests of Loyd and Gould have left the school’s community in shock, and two parents told News 6 that they plan to pull their children from the school effective immediately.

“They are no longer protecting our children. They are protecting the bad behaviors within that school,” parent Eleana Coscarelli told the outlet.

Both Coscarelli and fellow parent Stephenee Pearson remarked that they are frustrated with the lack of transparency from school leadership in light of the arrests.

“I think the answer is change and accountability and new leadership all around,” Pearson remarked.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and people are discovering all manner of little details in the game that speak to the developer's commitment to realism.
  • For starters, Jason has a home gym, and that's just smart on his part.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and people are discovering all manner of little details in the game that speak to the developer's commitment to realism. One such detail is the game's weightlifting and general fitness systems, and they seem to be pretty great, so much so that if you're thinking about getting into weight lifting, GTA 6's lessons are a good place to start. For starters, Jason has a home gym, and that's just smart on his part. Not having to leave your house and head to a gym is a godsend for anyone short on time or for those who simply enjoy the solitude of slinging weight around alone. For Jason, it's even better--he lives on the water, and it looks pretty damn serene heading to his workout pad for a sweat. If you're thinking about crafting your own home gym, Jason's setup is exactly what you need to get started: a squat rack, bench, kettlebells, barbells, and iron plates. Garage gym expert Cooper Mitchell also pointed out that Jason's squat stand uses 3"x3" uprights with 1" holes, and that's a great choice by Jason--or you--because it means you have universal support for other attachments from different brands that you might add over time.
