Tech Report: These Are the Best Ways to Encrypt Your Email

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (717 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that you probably already know that your email isn't actually all that private, especially if you have a free account with a major service provider like Gmail (Google) or Outlook (Microsoft).
  • Sources indicate that as this in-depth explainer from Adaptive Security describes, most emails are encrypted in transit via Transport Layer Security (TLS), which prevents anyone from reading your message as it travels from server to server.
  • Industry observers note that emails are also typically encrypted at rest—for example, while sitting on Google's servers and in a Gmail recipient's inbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you probably already know that your email isn't actually all that private, especially if you have a free account with a major service provider like Gmail (Google) or Outlook (Microsoft). But if you are sending sensitive information via email, you can minimize what can be snooped on and by whom using end-to-end encryption, which generally ensures that only the recipient can read your message. Here's what you need to know about email encryption and how to set up an extra layer of privacy.

Sources indicate that as this in-depth explainer from Adaptive Security describes, most emails are encrypted in transit via Transport Layer Security (TLS), which prevents anyone from reading your message as it travels from server to server. However, encryption is temporarily stripped at each server: content is received and processed in plaintext and then re-encrypted when it leaves, meaning it could be read, logged, and distributed by the server provider.

Industry observers note that emails are also typically encrypted at rest—for example, while sitting on Google's servers and in a Gmail recipient's inbox. But this only prevents someone with physical access to the server hardware from reading messages, as Google still holds the encryption key and can access stored data. And, as PCMag points out, Google is scanning your messages to a degree, and it (along with other email providers) can and will hand emails over to law enforcement and government agencies in some cases.

Recent findings suggest that by contrast, with end-to-end encryption (E2EE), emails are readable only on the sender's and recipient's devices, and can be decrypted only with the recipient's private key. They're never translated into plaintext as they pass between and through servers to their destination, meaning that no one—including server providers, hackers, or law enforcement—can view the content. It's worth noting, though, that E2EE is not impenetrable nor a total guarantee of privacy. For example, metadata like subject lines and email addresses may remain in plaintext, and encrypted messages are still susceptible to phishing. Plus, forwarding an encrypted message breaks the encryption.

Still, end-to-end encryption is especially useful when sending sensitive information that may be valuable to bad actors, though if security and privacy are a high priority, you may want to consider it for all of your emails. How you deploy encryption depends on whether you are adding it to your current email or switching to a dedicated provider.

If you have an account with a major email provider like Gmail, Outlook, or Apple Mail, you can add a third-party tool that layers an encryption protocol like OpenPGP on top of your existing account. PCMag recommends PreVeil, SecureMyEmail, and Virtru (which is limited to Gmail users in Chrome) for those who want to keep their current emails. Mailvelope is a browser add-on (and therefore a desktop-only tool) available in Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, though it can also be installed on other browsers, like Brave, that are built on the same architecture. FlowCrypt integrates with Gmail and Google Workspace on desktop and mobile.

Note that enterprise users of Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 have access to true end-to-end encryption without third-party add-ons. Gmail's Confidential mode and Outlook's Encrypt feature, available to all users, are not E2EE equivalents, as Google and Microsoft, respectively, still manage the keys.

Recent findings suggest that for those who are willing to start fresh with a latest email address (or who have a custom domain), providers like Proton Mail or Tuta offer native end-to-end encryption. The caveat: by default, this is only between people on the same service, so from one Proton user to another. If you want to send an end-to-end encrypted email from Proton to a Gmail user, for example, you have to set up password protection (and share the password via another secure channel) or use a PGP-compatible tool like those listed above. You can also Proton's Gmail integration does allow for end-to-end encryption, but only if both Gmail parties are using the Proton integration.

Recent findings suggest that the bottom line here is that email wasn't designed to be a highly secure form of communication. End-to-end encryption does add a layer of privacy and security if you jump through hoops to set it up, but it's still susceptible to human error and social engineering.

Even so, I was and am still the best goddamn driver in Leonida.

For instance, on that same first drive, at one point I was hanging out in a left-turn lane on a green light, yielding appropriately to oncoming traffic and waiting for it to pass so I could finish the turn.   • It has been revealed that hegseth was in a precarious position.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office. He asked his chief of staff whether she believed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth would survive the impeachment attempt that would soon be introduced by a member of his own party.

It has been revealed that hegseth was in a precarious position. He had been among the most aggressive champions of the war with Iran, widely seen as the policy most responsible for the shellacking Republicans had taken the night before. Wiles remained officially supportive of Hegseth throughout her time in the White House, but she had harbored concerns about the secretary from the start. She did not believe he was forthright about his skeletons during a rocky confirmation process, and she considered the subsequent Signalgate scandal an amateurish disaster.

It has been revealed that in the Wednesday meeting, according to a senior White House official, Wiles made clear that the war, the uncertainty of its next steps, and the inflation it had fueled all contributed to the midterms debacle. She offered her resignation, but Trump declined. On Thursday night, in a contentious meeting in the Oval Office, she offered to resign again. Trump confirmed the next day that Wiles would leave the White House for his outside political operation.

Sources indicate that hegseth’s fate was still uncertain. A deeply unpopular figure among the American public, presiding over an even more unpopular war, he faced an impeachment push led by Representative Thomas Massie. “He is just failing,” mentioned Republican senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina—who voted to confirm Hegseth at the start of Trump’s term—in an interview with Vanity Fair. “In the same way that Kristi Noem failed at Homeland Security, he simply doesn’t have the instincts or the prior experience as an executive that is necessary for this particular role.”.

In a recent development, the secretary of defense has now embarked on a campaign to save his job, and Stephen Miller’s elevation to replace Wiles as Trump’s chief of staff has helped to ensure a reprieve. Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.” And there are other reasons to keep him in place, the official said: Confirming a replacement will not be easy, particularly when Democrats take control of Congress, and ousting Hegseth would signal an admission that at this point, Trump’s war is a failure.

It was the president’s taste for staffers out of central casting that helped put Hegseth—a weekend morning television host with no experience in government, but with the square jaw of an Army Wives extra—in charge of the Department of Defense. He has relied on his talents before the cameras, and a team of advisers attuned to the production of his persona, to both keep his job and sell Trump on aggressive military action from the Pacific to the Persian Gulf. His survival has depended in part on his ability to project strength—not to the public, or to the rank-and-file, but to the president.

“In just under two years, Secretary Hegseth has worked side-by-side with President Trump to restore American power on the world stage, build the strongest military in generations, and instill a warrior ethos at the Pentagon,” White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales stated in a statement. “President Trump and Secretary Hegseth have taken bold, necessary action to deny the Iranian regime the ability to develop a nuclear weapon, bring narco-terrorist Nicolas Maduro to American justice, and defend our homeland from dangerous terrorists and cartels—saving American lives.”.

“They will stand behind him in the short term,” said a second senior administration official. And yet, “He is a cost. He’s constantly requiring people to spend political capital on him. The White House is constantly having to come in and save him. The question is, at what point is it too much of a cost to the president?”.

The morning after Hegseth survived the impeachment attempt, he attended a Veterans Day ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth was joined at the sacred memorial by his closest aides: Jennifer Hegseth, his third wife and a former Fox News producer who serves as an informal but influential adviser; his chief of staff Ricky Buria, a Marine Corps veteran who followed an unusual path into the top brass; and Tami Radabaugh, another former Fox News producer whom Hegseth hired as a senior adviser.

According to recent reports, as the group posed for photos at the Tomb, they chatted and laughed loudly. A US Army sentinel guarding the memorial turned to the group and shouted out a reprimand: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” After video of the moment made for embarrassing headlines, Hegseth awarded the soldier a Joint Service Commendation Medal and posed alongside several Army officers for a photoshoot that was posted on his social media accounts. The Pentagon did not elaborate on why a soldier was awarded a medal for an act as pedestrian as scolding noisy attendees at a memorial. “Hegseth would not have given him that award had the incident not been on TV,” remarked a former senior defense official.

The small group of advisers beside Hegseth has helped the secretary weather a series of scandals in his two years as defense secretary using stage-managed displays of toughness. “He’s a cross between a carnival barker and a personal trainer,” mentioned John Ullyot, who served as chief Pentagon spokesperson and senior adviser to Hegseth until he left the department last year. A loyal Trump backer, Ullyot initially supported Hegseth’s calls to restore standards and excise identity politics from the military. He has since emerged as a fierce public critic and now believes Hegseth should resign.

In his new book, The President Deserves Better, Ullyot describes a secretary of defense fixated on self-promotion and content creation. Jennifer plays an instrumental role in those efforts, directing the secretary’s social media and a small battalion of accounts that support him online. “It was as if she was producing him in his role as Secretary,” Ullyot writes. She has helped produce—and starred in—dramatic videos of Hegseth posted by the Pentagon’s official social media accounts. “Her entire job is to make his image,” one source told Vanity Fair.

House Republican Thomas Massie, who brought the articles of impeachment against Hegseth last week, argued the bombing was “the result of systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defense infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians.”.

Recent findings suggest that her role extended well beyond production, alarming senior officials in the Department of Defense. She interviewed candidates for Pentagon roles. She attended sensitive bilateral meetings with foreign officials. She was included in Signal chats that discussed the war plans for the Houthi operation in Yemen. The former defense official said they warned Hegseth about his wife’s involvement in Pentagon affairs. “She did not have a fucking clearance,” they said. “She shouldn’t be privy to this shit.”.

In a recent development, hegseth himself seemed too smitten to care. He covered the walls of his office, as well as other meeting rooms and corridors throughout the Pentagon, with large photos of himself and his wife. When The New York Times examined Jennifer’s influence at the department over the summer, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell called the former cable news producer “an accomplished leader.” He added that the Pentagon “not only welcomes her current leadership but actively plans to involve her even more deeply in the future.” Politico later reported that while advising the secretary of defense, Jennifer was being paid for consulting work by Watchtower Strategies, a Washington lobbying shop that counts Lockheed Martin as a client.

It has been revealed that she wasn’t the only Fox News producer at the Pentagon. Hegseth also gave Radabaugh—a former producer on Fox & Friends Weekend with no government experience—broad authority over department affairs, I’m told. Radabaugh made sure that glamorous photos and videos of Hegseth were published online promptly, sometimes scolding aides for taking too long to post. In the first few months of Hegseth’s tenure, she ordered Ullyot to turn a room just off the briefing room into a makeup studio.

“This was ridiculous. I remarked not only no, but hell no,” Ullyot writes. He warned that news of the makeup studio would leak. “How exactly did a makeup studio fit into the warrior ethos?”.

It has been revealed that in response to a detailed list of questions, Pentagon spokesman Joel Valdez declined to answer many of them but emailed a lengthy statement criticizing Ullyot. “There is no ‘makeup studio’ in the Pentagon, and it never existed,” Valdez remarked, going on to call Ullyot “a skinwalker,” a “sour puss coward,” and “generally a stupid person” who left “his job in disgrace.” (According to information reviewed by Vanity Fair, Hegseth praised Ullyot after his departure from the Pentagon and offered to recommend him to Susie Wiles, then Trump’s chief of staff.).

It has been revealed that “I volunteered to help stand up the Secretary’s press operation for a few months at the start of his term,” Ullyot told Vanity Fair in response. “I left as planned, and the Secretary thanked me for my work. My record over more than 30 years, including as a senior spokesman in the Senate and in the Trump White House, speaks for itself.”.

Hegseth was bullish on the war with Iran from the start. “There weren’t any real cheerleaders for the war in the cabinet outside of Pete Hegseth,” noted the second official. “It was Pete and [US Ambassador to Israel] Mike Huckabee.”.

Soon after his confirmation, Hegseth moved to increase his powers and consolidate control over the Pentagon. He ousted generals and subjected senior staff to polygraph tests to weed out leakers, a crusade that resulted in the abrupt firings of top officials that demoralized staff. He tapped Tim Parlatore, his personal lawyer, as a special adviser and charged him with overseeing leak investigations. Parlatore continued to run his own private practice as a criminal defense attorney, and Politico reported this week that while serving as Hegseth’s top adviser, he is representing the son of a Libyan warlord accused of extrajudicial killings and torture.

In keeping with the president’s broad campaign for retribution, Hegseth ordered an investigation into retired Joint Chiefs Chairman General Mark Milley, who had clashed with Trump during his first term, and stripped the four-star general of his security detail. The Pentagon is now working on a newly introduced report on the 2021 Kabul Airport attack, during which 13 American soldiers and 170 Afghan civilians were killed in a suicide bombing during the withdrawal from Afghanistan. At the time, Milley served as chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The new assessment, one source familiar with the investigation noted, is expected by the end of the month and is intended to serve as a predicate to strip Milley of his four-star rank.

Recent findings suggest that hegseth waged a parallel war on the press, starting with an attempt to ban NBC News correspondent Courtney Kube from the Pentagon. In a meeting with his advisers, Ullyot writes, Hegseth explained that he and his wife Jennifer were “angry” at Kube for how much she covered his turbulent confirmation process before Congress. “I thought this was loony tunes,” Ullyot writes. One source told me that after NBC News was kicked out of its Pentagon office, Hegseth aides took a full-length mirror from the vacated room and installed it in his makeup studio.

Sources indicate that as Hegseth purged senior officials, he grew closer to Buria. The relationship was confounding to many inside the building: Hegseth has pushed to cleanse the Pentagon of ideological diversity, yet he elevated Buria, a holdover from the Biden administration who had previously donated to Democrats. But Buria had earned the trust of Jennifer. When explaining to advisers why he was elevated, Hegseth said he prayed about the decision with his wife. “And you know what? Jen notes he’s really good with the kids,” Hegseth told them.

Buria was by Hegseth’s side throughout the Signalgate scandal, which, according to several administration officials, was a turning point for the secretary. “Every problem he is having in one way or another goes back to Signalgate,” the second Trump official said. “His extremely hostile relations with the press, his paranoia, his firing of certain people, denied promotions to generals. It was all around paranoia related to Signalgate.”.

“There’s two versions of Hegseth,” stated a second former defense official. “There is the pre-Signalgate version and the post-Signalgate version. It’s like Jekyll and Hyde. He was Dr. Jekyll until around Signalgate, and he’s been Mr. Hyde ever since. He’s just not making good decisions.”.

It was an almost unbelievable incident: Hegseth shared war prepares for a bombing campaign against the Houthis in Yemen on at least two Signal group chats, including one that inadvertently included Jeffrey Goldberg, the editor in chief of The Atlantic.

This was the first major military engagement of Hegseth’s tenure, but he chose to survey the operation with Buria from a temporary secure facility at his Fort McNair home rather than make the short trip to the Pentagon or the White House Situation Room. The decision alarmed some at the Pentagon. “It’s your first major military operation,” said the second senior Trump official. “Why would you monitor it from your shitty SCIF in your basement? Why not go 10 minutes to the Pentagon where you have the joint staff?”.

“You would think with kinetic operations going on in the Middle East that could have dramatic consequences for service members, that he’d be in the office,” Tillis mentioned.

Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.”.

It has been revealed that during Hegseth’s confirmation process, allegations of heavy drinking concerned Republican lawmakers he needed to vote in favor of his nomination. At the time, several Republican senators said he promised them he would stop boozing if confirmed. He affirmed this pledge publicly: “This is the biggest deployment of my life,” he told Megyn Kelly in a 2024 interview, “and there won’t be a drop of alcohol on my lips while I’m doing it.”.

Whether or not Hegseth has actually quit drinking continues to be a source of palace intrigue. One official recalled watching Hegseth drink what the secretary suggested were two cocktails—though the official conceded he hadn’t seen the drinks poured, and raised a theory that Hegseth might have been testing whether he would leak the incident to the press. “This was at a time of peak paranoia,” the official said.

It has been revealed that buria was known to drink on official trips; the official recalled Hegseth’s aide handing out shots to passengers on a US government jet during a Pentagon junket. Two other officials remarked Buria would often brag about drinking with Hegseth, including on an official trip to Panama in 2025. The New York Post later reported that Buria had made up a story about him and Hegseth donning disguises to go out and drink, all in an effort to weed out leakers. One of the officials told me they believed the leak claim was Buria’s retroactive effort to cover up that he was boasting about drinking with the secretary.

“The drinking is what they’re really afraid of,” the second official noted. When asked directly if Hegseth continued drinking as secretary, a Defense Department spokesperson who declined to be named said in a statement: “No, the Secretary has kept his promise that he made during his confirmation hearings and has not drank since becoming Secretary of War.”.

Jennifer and Pete Hegseth have forged a close relationship with Stephen Miller and his wife Katie, their neighbors on a placid and heavily fortified army base south of the White House. Hegseth’s temporary salvation comes thanks in part to support from Miller, who values his deference to Trump. “Stephen doesn’t like all the Liberace shit, the cucaracha shit,” mentioned the first former official. “Pete right now is fresh out of friends, and misery loves company. But don’t get it twisted. At any moment, at any second, Stephen will cut Pete’s throat.”.

The secretary of defense has made few friends in Washington. One source recalled attending a holiday party stocked with members of the administration during which Hegseth spent much of his time alone in the corner of the room. “Even Kash Patel had people coming up to him to talk,” the source noted. “Pete was alone and isolated. He looked depressed. And this was before the Iran war. His stock has not gone up since then.”.

Industry observers note that hegseth has channeled much of his effort into appealing to an audience of one, telling advisers he only cares about Trump’s opinion. “The one thing he’s been successful at, and I think it’s the only thing, is flattering Donald Trump constantly,” the former official remarked.

Industry observers note that the purpose of this flattery campaign extends beyond keeping his current job. In private, Hegseth has confided in several officials about his ambitions to run for president. This jockeying has exacerbated tensions with Vice President JD Vance. The relationship was already strained by Vance’s private opposition to the Iran war, and it deteriorated significantly after the vice president’s close friend, Dan Driscoll, was pushed out of his position as Army Secretary in August following months of friction with Hegseth.

Sources indicate that when explaining to advisers why Buria was elevated, Hegseth noted he prayed about the decision with his wife. “And you know what? Jen says he’s really good with the kids,” Hegseth told them.

“Secretary Hegseth and Vice President Vance share an outstanding working relationship grounded in deep mutual respect and alignment,” Parnell remarked in a statement to Vanity Fair.

Jennifer has worked in tandem with her husband to push allies on social media and in the press to promote the idea of a presidential run. “She wants to be first lady,” the former official noted of Jennifer. “She wants to be Hillary.” After the midterms, online influencers whom Hegseth hired earlier this year to work as special government employees at the Pentagon began pitching Hegseth for president. These influencers were nominally hired to promote Hegseth’s efforts to bring war colleges in line with the “warrior ethos,” but in reality they coordinated with Jennifer and Radabaugh on “shitposting,” the second official said. Earlier this month, they rallied to Hegseth’s defense as he came under fire for the Republican ballot box-bloodbath, posting action shots of the secretary with the caption: “STAND. FIGHT. DEFEND THE REPUBLIC.”.

These influencers often attack journalists who cover the Pentagon. In response to a recent story by Politico’s Daniel Lippman, an active-duty Army officer known as InfantryDort on social media—whom Hegseth hired as one of these shadow spokespeople—posted: “I expect you all to ratio the fuck out of this retard and in short order. Daniel Lippman remains absolute journalistic filth.” A Politico spokesperson responded: “Daniel is one of Washington’s best-sourced reporters, and we’re lucky to have him at POLITICO.”.

When Democrats take control of Congress, they are expected to focus much of their oversight on Hegseth, including the scandals from his personal life. The subjects broached in his contentious confirmation hearings—including an affidavit signed by his former sister-in-law alleging abuse against his second wife—are likely to be relitigated. (His second wife denied that she was physically abused.).

“Is that going to be good for the president?” Tillis asked. “His entire confirmation will be re-prosecuted. That affidavit will get a lot of attention. Family members will most likely be subpoenaed. Does he really want to go through that at a personal level, and at the same time be such a massive disruption for the leader of the most lethal, complex organization in American government? Is this about Pete, or is this about America’s defense? I don’t know how any objective person can say that the value that he brings is greater than that distraction and the cost of him remaining in place.”.

According to recent reports, “If he had any dignity, he would resign and allow the president to appoint a replacement in the lame duck session,” said the first official. “But he doesn’t.”.

Hegseth’s ability to project confidence is not confined to the cameras. He was bullish on the war with Iran from the start. “There weren’t any real cheerleaders for the war in the cabinet outside of Pete Hegseth,” said the second official. “It was Pete and [US Ambassador to Israel] Mike Huckabee.” In late December 2025, Hegseth met with Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the Four Seasons in Palm Beach shortly before Netanyahu ventured to Mar-a-Lago to make the case for fresh strikes on Iran. By February, Netanyahu was pushing Trump to join Israel in a full-blown war to topple the Iranian regime.

Hegseth was all-in, his confidence buoyed by the success of Operation Midnight Hammer—a series of strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025—and the raid to abduct Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro. His allies in the administration point to these operations, as well as a post-pandemic surge in military recruitment numbers, as his major successes in the job.

But multiple officials who spoke with Vanity Fair said they believed that when briefing Trump, Hegseth understated the risks of war with Iran from the beginning and went on to overstate its successes as the conflict dragged on. “Pete gave the rosiest picture in the world,” said the first former official. During early discussions about potentially launching the war, the official said they were struck by how quickly Hegseth started speaking about the operation as a “foregone conclusion.”.

In a recent development, “Leading up into the war, he presented, along with [Central Command Commander Admiral] Brad Cooper, overly optimistic projections of what the air campaign could achieve,” mentioned the second administration official. “This is how the president got this idea that it could be done in a matter of two to three weeks.”.

According to recent reports, hegseth ran against Democrat U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar in 2012.

Tillis, for his part, noted that he did not believe Hegseth was forthright with Trump about the war. “He planned the good, bright, shiny stuff that was Epic Fury, but clearly did not brief the president on things that anybody that’s had any experience in the Middle East knows,” Tillis added. “The first thing that goes is the Strait of Hormuz.”.

“Secretary Hegseth and Pentagon leadership consistently provide the President with the complete, unvarnished picture so he can make the best choices for America’s security and success,” Parnell said in a statement.

On the first day of the war, a missile struck the Minab elementary school in southern Iran, killing more than 150 people, the majority of them children. The US military has thus far refused to publicly admit responsibility for the strike, despite a preliminary military investigation concluding within days of the strike that a US missile struck the school. Before the attack, Hegseth gutted the Pentagon program aimed at reducing civilian harm during military operations, ProPublica reported in March. House Republican Thomas Massie, who brought the articles of impeachment against Hegseth last week, argued the bombing was “the result of systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defense infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians.”.

Massie cast the strike as a consequence of Hegseth’s oft-repeated mantra: “Maximum lethality, not tepid legality.”.

As the war went on, officials said, Hegseth continued to trumpet its successes, showing the president what one official described as “hype videos” depicting strikes on missile launchers, Iranian ships, and old aircraft. Hegseth told Trump “that the majority of Iran’s missile capabilities and the majority of Iran’s Air Force was destroyed,” the official said, even though US intelligence “highlighted that wasn’t the case, and that the majority of Iran’s missiles and missile launchers by the end of the major combat phase of the war were still intact.”.

“He creates an echo chamber in the press corps so that he can get only nice questions or do made-for-TV stuff,” stated Senator Tillis.

Hegseth also worked behind the scenes to promote positive media coverage of the war. He briefed Fox News hosts whom he remained friendly with on the war’s progress and encouraged them to present a positive picture on air. But Hegseth himself has made little effort to explain or defend the war to Americans. Even as the war has become a political debacle for the administration, he remains bullish on escalation. “Pete is the only one who wants to restart strikes,” the first official said.

In a recent development, we were all sitting in our assigned seats waiting for the performance to start when a security official walked into the Pentagon briefing room to make an announcement. Hegseth had not held a Pentagon press briefing since May. Now, facing an impeachment effort from a member of his own party, he came before the cameras. “If anyone gets out of line today, you’re going to be physically removed,” the official said. “Is that clear?”.

“Sense of decorum,” the official remarked apologetically. “Just be professional.”.

In a recent development, the official noted he was just relaying orders from Hegseth’s office. A few minutes later, Joel Valdez, the press aide, walked out and asked if anyone was confused. Everyone was. “I could tell you off the record?” he said. No, the reporters replied. “Do you want to hear it off the record?” No, they said again.

Valdez looked down at his shoes and then walked out of the room without saying another word. “In my 30 years in DC, I have never heard that,” stated a cameraman. “This is crazytown.”.

Industry observers note that at 8 a.m. sharp, Hegseth walked out wearing a loud plaid suit, a striped tie, and an American flag pocket square. The timing is no coincidence; officials stated Hegseth schedules briefings in the 8 a.m. hour because Trump is known to watch Fox News at that time.

The secretary of defense began reading his speech from a stack of papers on the podium. From my assigned seat in the back row, I felt as if I were watching an interpretive dance. The choreography of Hegseth’s hand movements and facial expressions was as slick as his hair, which was gelled into a stiff meringue that moved in unison with his tanned face.

Hegseth punctuated a line about President Trump’s “decisive” leadership with a clenched fist thrust downward. The word “overseeing” was expressed with a slow swipe of the hand over an imaginary stretch of purview. As Hegseth recalled the glories of the Maduro operation—and, parenthetically, his part in directing them—he dismissed criticism of the raid by leaning into the microphone, shaking his head from side to side and wiggling his eyebrows: “It wasn’t”—dramatic pause for eyebrow wiggle—“a kidnapping.”.

Hegseth's presser had a pantomime quality.

The briefing itself exuded little of the confidence Hegseth sought to signal before the cameras. He took seven questions in total, sticking to friendly reporters in the front rows who had signed a pledge in September 2025 to not report “unauthorized information” from the Pentagon. One of them, a representative of Real America’s Voice, asked “what message” is sent to America’s allies when “our own politicians don’t support taking out the narco traffickers that kill their own constituents?” It wasn’t so much a question as a warm bath. Some in the room, visibly frustrated by the waste of time, rolled their eyes. Others shouted questions from the back about Iran and impeachment. Hegseth refused to look at them.

“He creates an echo chamber in the press corps so that he can get only nice questions or do made-for-TV stuff,” said Tillis, who also decried Hegseth for filming a slick video of himself outside the Department of Defense making the case for why he should not be impeached: “He demonstrated more impulsiveness by using taxpayer dollars to defend himself against impeachment.”.

In his remarks before the press, Hegseth framed the effort to remove him as an attack on the troops. “If they want to come for the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me,” he stated, jabbing a finger into his chest. But the impeachment targeted Hegseth, not “the warriors.” We had assembled to hear Pete make the case for Pete. Indeed, he had not held a press briefing when a Navy commander died in a helicopter crash on July 1, or when three US soldiers were killed in an Iranian strike on a base in Jordan on July 17. What brought him back before the cameras was not the ongoing war in the Middle East but his own fight to save his career here in Washington.

Recent findings suggest that the performance earned a rave review from the one viewer who mattered. “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

In a recent development, early on in Hegseth’s tenure, he confided in advisers about his “biggest fear” as he took on the mighty responsibility of leading the Department of Defense, the first former official told me: “Being fired and embarrassed.” For now, Trump is standing by his secretary. He always is, until he isn’t. When asked just before the midterms whether Wiles would remain on as his chief of staff, Trump said there was “zero chance” he’d replace her. Three weeks later, she was out.

Breaking: More Mass Layoffs At Ubisoft Underway, Affecting Two Of Its Biggest Studios

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (610 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, ubisoft has enacted another round of mass layoffs, affecting 166 additional jobs as the French gaming giant continues its cost-cutting program.
  • Ubisoft has enacted another round of mass layoffs, affecting 166 additional jobs as the French gaming giant continues its cost-cutting program.
  • Sources indicate that the job cuts are happening at two of Ubisoft's biggest development hubs in Montreal and Quebec.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ubisoft has enacted another round of mass layoffs, affecting 166 additional jobs as the French gaming giant continues its cost-cutting program. The job cuts are happening at two of Ubisoft's biggest development hubs in Montreal and Quebec. A spokesperson for Ubisoft said the job cuts are coming to meet changing production needs, and IGN reported that the layoffs came from teams working on projects that have been "canceled or refocused." "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect," the spokesperson said. "Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources." Ubisoft Montreal is right now working on Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe, while Ubisoft Quebec most recently debuted Assassin's Creed Shadows. No further updates are coming to that game, leaving the question of what the team is making next. In October, Ubisoft said there are no additional Assassin's Creed remakes currently in development, following the release of Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag Resynced earlier this year. “Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin’s Creed titles, including projects you haven’t heard about yet, featuring latest settings and stories," the developer said. Ubisoft's restructuring has led to several canceled games, shut-down studios, and layoffs. Trials developer RedLynx is on the chopping block, while 72 people from Ubisoft Singapore–the studio behind Skull & Bones–were recently laid off. Just today, November 19, Ubisoft released its latest earnings report that mentioned that Ubisoft's third phase of its cost-reduction program remains "firmly on track." Ubisoft is targeting €1.25 billion ($1.37 billion) in cost reductions by March 2028, so it's possible there will be more pain in the firm's future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vanderpump Rules alum Scheana Shay and her husband, Brock Davies, have been discussing whether to expand their family.

In a recent development, “This is something we’ve been talking about a little more lately,” Scheana, 41, said on a recent episode of her “Scheananigans” podcast. “I’ve been back and forth with if we want another kid, if we want to do a surrogate and all of that.”.

Recent findings suggest that scheana and Brock, 36, welcomed daughter Summer Moon in 2021. (Brock is also the father of two older children from a previous relationship, from whom he is estranged.).

It has been revealed that “There was a friend of mine’s dad’s funeral that we were at [in] the beginning of this year,” Scheana tearfully recalled on her podcast. “Seeing her stand up there with her two siblings, I just knew when that moment comes for Summer, I want her to have someone. I don’t want her to be up there alone.”.

The former Bravo star and Brock have yet to officially make plans to have another child.

According to recent reports, “However, I’m not necessarily ready to take that next step yet,” Scheana noted. “Summer also, right now, is in this only-child phase where she does not want to share me.”.

Should Scheana and Brock decide to move forward with expanding their brood, the reality TV alum has stated that she wouldn’t carry their child after complications from her last pregnancy.

“HELLP [Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes and Low Platelet count] syndrome can be fatal. It’s something most people don’t know about,” she exclusively told Us in her July 2025 cover story. “I certainly didn’t until I was transferred to the high-risk ICU. When Summer was born and not making a sound, I was terrified. I thought she wasn’t going to make it. It was the scariest minute of my entire life.”.

At the time, Scheana admittedly hadn’t yet “fully come to terms with” using a gestational carrier to potentially welcome another baby.

According to recent reports, “I felt [Summer] kick, I felt her hiccup, I breastfed her, and it’s going to be a very different experience this time,” she told Us. “I worry that I might not have the same connection to the baby, but we are slowly taking steps in that direction.”.

In a recent development, “It takes work every single day. I will forever have insecurities,” she told Us. “Just the other day, I saw him swipe and delete a text, and I’m like, ‘What was that?’ And he’s like, ‘Seriously, Scheana?’ I genuinely believe he would never do anything like that again. I do trust him. I have forgiven him.”.

10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that apple has a pretty good track record on privacy.
  • It has been revealed that enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device.
  • Another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple has a pretty good track record on privacy. The company bakes a number of protections into its OSes to keep your data from being shared or stolen. That noted, you can make your Apple devices even more secure. There are plenty of opt-in settings that make it even harder for anyone to snoop on your device and activity. These are the best privacy hacks for your Mac.

It has been revealed that enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device. Turning on Stealth Mode prevents your Mac from even responding to these requests, essentially making it invisible to anything that's scanning a network you're connected to. This makes it more difficult for hackers and malware to know your device exists, much less attack it. This can interfere with certain essential activity when you're on your home network, but it's a valuable security setting when on public wifi. You can leave Firewall on all the time and enable Stealth Mode only as needed. Go to Settings > Network > Firewall, flip the toggle, then hit Options to manage Stealth Mode.

Another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi. If you use either your real MAC address or a fixed one (random but unchanging), it's easier to track your activity on that network, including when you arrive, how long you stay, and when you leave. Rotating addresses are best for public, shared networks you temporarily connect to, and don't require a login via a captive portal (like hotel wifi). You can turn this on for specific networks via Settings > Wi-Fi > [Network Name] > Details and change Private Wi-Fi address to Rotating.

Images and screenshots contain metadata, such as timestamps, device and hardware details, and, in the case of photos, physical location. Much of this information is stripped automatically when you share files to social media or via encrypted messaging apps, but if you're sending them via text or email, posting to forums, or sharing over AirDrop, metadata remains intact. You can easily remove metadata from your images right on your desktop. Select the file and hit control + click to bring up an options menu, then go to Quick Actions > Convert Image. Uncheck the box next to Preserve Metadata, then hit Convert. (This is also useful for rapidly converting HEIC to JPEG without opening a separate app.).

Apple collects information about your device for diagnostic purposes or to improve apps and services, some of which is shared with third-party app developers. This may include crash and usage data as well as recordings and transcripts of Siri interactions and iCloud analytics. You can disable sharing for some or all of these categories under Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

You may be surprised by the number of apps and system services that use your device's location in the background. You should definitely disable location services for third-party apps that don't require location to function. You can find these toggles under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services. You can also turn off location permissions for some Apple apps and services if you're not using them on your device, like Weather and Maps. Finally, tap System Services and disable location for any non-essential features—at the very least, disable "Mac Analytics" and "Significant Locations & routes" (which lets your Mac and other iCloud devices learn locations and routes you use often).

Third-party apps on your Mac that need access to your device's camera and microphone have to request permission, and it's easy to grant this in the moment and then forget that you've allowed it. You should regularly audit which apps have these permissions and revoke access from those that don't need them on a day-to-day basis. Disabling them forces the app to ask again. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone or Camera to see the allowed apps and flip the toggle to disable permissions.

It has been revealed that another permission type you may have granted without much thought is local network access. This allows third-party apps to discover and communicate with other devices—printers, smart speakers, and IoT devices—on your home wifi. While this may be useful for services like Spotify that cast to connected hardware, other utilities, media apps, and games probably don't need to be mapping your network in the background. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network to audit permissions and disable those that aren't needed.

Recent findings suggest that another vital permission to check concerns third-party apps that have access to your Mac's full disk, which includes data from Mail, Messages, Safari, Home, Time Machine, and admin settings. If an app only works with files you explicitly open and save, it doesn't need full disk access. Legitimate use cases may include antivirus and malware scanners, productivity tools, or backup utilities that you trust. You can also audit which apps have access to specific files and folders. This is under Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access or Files & Folders.

Recent findings suggest that if you're using iCloud to store photos, files, and device backups, your data is encrypted on Apple's servers and in transit. Apple still holds the decryption key, which is useful if you somehow get locked out of your account and need help recovering it, but for sensitive data—including device backups—end-to-end encryption is the most secure way to ensure no one but you can gain access. Advanced Data Protection is an opt-in setting for iCloud that encrypts your information end to end. You'll need to set up an alternative recovery method, such as your device passcode with two-factor authentication, a recovery contact, or a recovery key. Be careful, though: If you lose access to this recovery method, you will lose your data. You can enable Advanced Data Protection on your Mac under System Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Advanced Data Protection > Turn On. Note that some iCloud data, including passwords and payment methods, are already end-to-end encrypted by default.

  • To change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings, move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. He's a good sport when I make him wear the dumbest graphic tees I can find. For a gunslinging drug runner, he's a gentle soul. I just have one complaint.

The man's got a leisurely gait. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button.

To change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings, move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. The setting you're looking for is Movement Speed.

This doesn't affect your top speed while sprinting and burning stamina. What it adjusts is the speed you move at when you fully push the joystick. There are four options, each one offering more speed than the last: Walk (the default), Fast Walk, Jog, and Run.

According to recent reports, it's a nice bit of granularity. I go with Fast Walk to give just a slight bump in my base speed without feeling like I'm rushing, but Jog or Run are good options if you really want to cover ground. Whichever one you choose, you can still voluntarily move at a slower pace by only slightly tilting the joystick.

There's also a Combat Movement Speed setting, which—as you might expect—changes the pace you walk at in a gunfight. There are only three options here: Fast Walk, Jog, and Run, because nobody wants to move slowly when they're actively being shot at.

While you're in the menus, I'd recommend digging around to inspect all the available options. Rockstar included a lot of toggles and tweaks for fine-tuning how GTA 6 handles. You can even turn off vehicle damage altogether, if you don't want to pay for car repairs. Not that I've ever crashed or anything. Don't ask my mechanic.

#17040. WoW: Forever Wants To Get Rid Of The Idea Of “BiS” Gear

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1453 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamespot ↗ Open Full Page

WoW: Forever Wants To Get Rid Of The Idea Of “BiS” Gear

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1453 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's latest items, class changes, and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices. In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's fresh items, class changes, and more. On the subject of raid gear and chase items, Forever senior game designer Aidan Moon said something that could be seen as controversial in certain circles of the game's community. "I essentially want to get rid of BiS," Moon said. "I think that BiS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about [the] role-playing aspects of it." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=67dDe3QgJtM BiS is WoW shorthand for essentially the best item that could possibly be in a given gear slot for a specific class. Look up any WoW guide for WoW Classic or modern WoW, and you'll find class BiS gear lists telling players exactly what they should be wearing in order for their character to be as powerful as possible. Endgame in many ways revolves around acquiring your BiS gear, first your "pre-raid" BiS from gear available in max-level dungeons, and then BiS gear, like tier sets, from raids. It's for that exact reason Forever introduced new items that grant additional stats or effects against certain enemy types or even in certain locations. Moon gave an example of specific items that deal more damage against Murloc enemies, and that players might want to have more gear tailored to fighting against a Murloc boss in a raid encounter. Forever's raids will feature multiple distinct biomes within them, Moon revealed, giving players more factors to consider when choosing what gear to use for specific parts of each raid. One wing of a raid may be snowy, while another may be cavernous, changing what gear could be more optimal for those encounters. "I think your BiS should be different [for] every single boss if you're actually making a theoretical BiS list," Moon said. "It should be based on the creature and the biome and a mixture of those two. You might have an item that's really good against snowy, and then another item in that same slot that's really good against Murlocs. Then there's a Murloc boss in a snowy area and you're just like 'Which one do I wear?' And then eventually you get to a point where you're swapping those things out or it's too much cognitive load and you don't want to do that. It's for those players that really want to optimize."  Trying to get rid of BiS lists is a significant change for WoW, which has revolved around the idea for over two decades. Players can already encounter some of the itemization ideas Moon discussed while leveling to 60, with low-level gear from dungeons and quests dealing more damage against specified enemy types or even granting additional movement speed in specific zones. "I don't want you to have to ever think about BiS, I just want you to think about the fight right in front of you and how you're going to fight it," Moon said. Of course, having more biome- or enemy-type-specific items means hoarding more pieces of gear as opposed to selling old ones when an upgrade comes around. That will no doubt promptly fill up the inventories and banks of players looking to min-max for every possible scenario. Classic WoW is already notorious for having limited bag space, and players running around with multiple sets of hyper-specific gear will only make that pain point worse. Blizzard sounds like it's aware of that problem. Principal game designer Kris Zierhut said bigger bags are on that way, but that it's not needed right now immediately post-launch. However, Blizzard knows players will eventually need more bag space as well as better ways to organize and search for owned items to make putting together encounter-specific sets of gear easier. It's a massive change, but the strategy Blizzard is employing seems to be working. Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent and weekly player records, and more than 15 million characters have been created in the MMO so far. Blizzard recently lifted the veil on how Forever's new PvP system will work, revealing how classic WoW's infamous rank grind will now be a thing of the past.

A Survivor Legend Went Off About The Coin Flip, And Honestly She’s Right

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A lot of Survivor fans are still in their feels about the coin flip, and let the record show, fan favorite and multi-time player Kelley Wentworth is among the frustrated.
  • During her extended rant, Wentworth ran down a laundry list of concerns.
  • According to recent reports, I don’t like the coin flip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A lot of Survivor fans are still in their feels about the coin flip, and let the record show, fan favorite and multi-time player Kelley Wentworth is among the frustrated. She dropped a video yesterday going off about the game mechanic and talking through in very specific detail exactly why she wants it gone.

During her extended rant, Wentworth ran down a laundry list of concerns. She brought up how Lewis apparently won the coin toss but then was told it didn’t count because it landed outside the little circular mat host Jeff Probst had put down. She brought up how every single fan with any time awareness knew he was going to lose the coin flip because there wasn’t enough time left in the episode to vote. And more broadly, she brought up the fact that we’re never going to be able to recreate the special circumstances of the original coin flip with Rick Devens on 50, so what’s the point in trying. You can read her blunt words about that below….

According to recent reports, I don’t like the coin flip. I don’t like it. We should have left that in season 50 along with Mr. Beast and Rick Devens flipping it. This coin flip was only fun in 50 because of all the circumstances, because it was Mr. Beast and it was so ridiculous, because it was Rick and he was on the bottom and he was so excited about doing it and it actually worked. Yes, this is a very results based twist, but bringing this back in 51 and now we’re carrying it into other seasons? No. This did not hit the same. I don’t like it. I don’t care about the increased prize money. This was just depressing.

She’s obviously right. I wasn’t a huge fan of the coin flip on 50. I could see where the show was coming from though because it felt like a grandiose, over the top one-off moment that matched a milestone season and a fun, reckless player always willing to gamble. The circumstances just worked, even if it’s not a game mechanic I personally would have designed.

This season, however, it felt really forced and out of place. We’ve been getting banger tribal council after banger tribal council with some of the most interesting votes in the history of the show. What most of us wanted, as fans, was just to watch the players do that again, but instead, we lost one of the season’s most entertaining characters on a freakin’ coin flip. As Wentworth put it, it’s just depressing.

You can watch her full rant in all its glory below….

A post shared by kelleywentworth (@kelleywentworth).

Survivor has already revealed that the coin flip is coming back for future seasons. During Survivor 52, one player will flip for the chance to push the prize pot to three million dollars. I hope it hits, and then I hope the producers take a look at the coin flip and its future in the game.

Industry observers note that like Wentworth, I’d personally like to see it removed, but if the show is going to keep it, they should at least experiment with a different structure and/ or different rules. Maybe one player can decide at any point after jury to flip it, and they just announce it at tribal. Maybe all the players vote and then someone decides whether they want to negate it. Maybe it’s a one-time option the players are allowed to pass on. Maybe a player wins an advantage and they personally get to decide whether to flip it or not flip it.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Regardless, I’m going to stay positive on Survivor 51. Yes, the coin flip was a big bummer. Yes, it was devastating to lose Lewis, but even so, this is the best season we’ve gotten in a long time. The cast is half crazies and half schemers, and there are already like five moments that will be referenced for years to come, including Brady’s chopped finger, the most embarrassing quit in show history, Kilby standing on business and the blindside of poor Pantsless Patt. Fingers crossed the rest of the season gives us a few more and in doing so, solidifies its place as an all-time great season.

As it turns out, the dog looks to be based on a real-life dog named Loosy who does neat stunts in Florida. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

Sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel users are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November revision apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

Industry observers note that here's the situation: Following the November revision, some customers are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the problem is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

Industry observers note that to be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal matter. It's not like all Pixel owners are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

Sources indicate that luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some owners are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

What does appear to work, however, is shutting your Pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

If your Pixel's camera is giving you grief following the November update, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. As the issue does seem to be rather widespread, I wouldn't be surprised to see Google issue a patch in the coming days. But until then, turning your phone off for five minutes may be a decent compromise.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a tale as old as time: amass a fortune with hard work, lose the fortune with reckless spending. That’s certainly true of Johnny Depp, whose latest movie, Ebenezer, is in theaters now on the 2026 movie schedule. Depp has gone through a lot of ups and downs in the last couple of decades, since becoming one of the highest-paid actors in Hollywood with the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise, starting in the summer of 2003. Now, a new biography about Depp is getting into some of the details of his fortune made and lost, and the numbers, as you might expect, are staggering.

In the fresh book, The Many Faces of Johnny Depp, author Mark Seal notes that court documents from 2017 let us in on just how staggering the numbers are. Depp has admitted to being hundreds of millions in the hole, but the new book touches more on where that money went and how he spent so much, so swiftly. Of course, there are quite a few reasons, but they can be summed up in two, according to Seal. He writes (via PageSix):.

His vast wealth had been gutted, fittingly, in a Jack Sparrow-like bacchanal of excessive spending and financial mismanagement.

That spending, according to PageSix, included buying a luxury yacht, 14 homes, pricey cases of wine, jewelry, and a private island in the Bahamas. He also spent lavishly on travel and the people who surrounded him at the height of his earnings and fame. Seal writes:.

[He] didn’t move without an entourage and could never again fly on a commercial airline … He was no longer merely Johnny — he was Johnny Depp, mega-movie star, icon, brand, and franchise, with an expanding army of people depending on him for their livelihoods.

As Depp has admitted, he was also on the hook for $100 million in back taxes owed to Uncle Sam, a debt he blamed on the accountants and advisors he thought were paying the taxes when they apparently weren’t.

It has been revealed that in the years since his court battle with Amber Heard, Depp’s reputation has taken a major hit, and that has also impacted his finances. For Ebenezer, Depp took a major cut from what he was earning for movies a decade ago. He apparently earned a “mere” $5 million for the fresh take on A Christmas Carol. That’s a lot of coin, for sure, but when you compare that to the $90 million Depp reportedly earned for Dead Men Tell No Tales, and the $16 million paycheck he received for Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald (a movie he was promptly cut from), you get the full picture.

The entertainment and sports worlds are filled with stories like this, and Depp isn’t all that unique, though the numbers involved are still eye-popping. There are also growing rumors that Depp could eventually return as Jack Sparrow, but that seems a long way off, even if they are true. Time will tell if Depp can ever start earning money like he used to.

But apparently, some members of the development team still don’t know how the game ends.

In Toby Fox’s autumn 2026 Deltarune newsletter, he provided an patch on the status of Chapter 7 as follows:.

In a recent development, I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped readingâ¦ I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens.

Everyone agrees it’s more fun this way.

In a recent development, team members who completed their work on Chapter 6 have moved onto Chapter 7 now. Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I’m doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence…!

So essentially, the Deltarune developers are working on early parts of Chapter 7 without knowing what the entire chapter entails. Ridiculous as this sounds on its face, it makes a little bit of sense given the intricate way Deltarune‘s story has played out and how much speculation there is about how it will end. I really mean it when I say it’s impossible to predict what’s going to happen in this one, particularly with regard to the game’s two (three?) different paths, and its overall themes of breaking free from one’s destiny. And if you’ve played Undertale, you know how Fox likes to mess with player expectations!

Industry observers note that elsewhere in the newsletter, Fox confirms that Chapter 6 has begun localization and preliminary testing and is playable from beginning to end. It’s sounding more and more like we’ll see Chapter 6 in 2027, given the pace that Chapter 5’s development took.

(And I still think there’s going to be a Chapter 8 after all this, but that’s just my personal fantheory.).

Good afternoon from Washington, where Party Animals has not forgotten the 5 a.m. wake-up required last Tuesday to attend Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s first Pentagon press conference in six months. This was a peculiar one, arranged so Hegseth could brief the public on his own personal battle for career survival.

Industry observers note that the briefing kicked off at 8 a.m., but the press had to be at the Pentagon by 6 a.m. for an extensive security screening. I’d like to think that this cruel early start was a consequence of Hegseth’s self-proclaimed sobriety. What kind of drunk drags his sorry carcass before a crowd of jackals before noon? Not any I know.

But sources I spoke with for a newly introduced piece on Hegseth’s war inside the Pentagon told me there was a more Machiavellian motivation for the presser: Donald Trump loves to watch Fox & Friends at 8 a.m. And sure enough, soon after the conclusion of Hegseth’s performance, its intended audience of one offered a review on Truth Social.

Read on for my investigation into Hegseth’s turbulent tenure at the top of the Department of Defense, and what it means for his survival as Democrats take control of Congress in January.

The reviews are in for Joe Biden’s fresh book, Promise Me, America. The Atlantic calls the book “unrepentant.” The New York Times calls it a 400-page “cover letter.” The former president offers the fantastical opinion that he should have stayed in the race in 2024 and faced Trump, quite a position to maintain given he couldn’t voice his own audiobook and limited his press appearances for the release to a soft-focus People magazine story (his publisher did not respond to Party Animals’ multiple requests for an interview). According to the reviews, the former president dedicates scant attention to one of the biggest debacles of his presidency, the war in Gaza, which he abetted thanks to near-unwavering support for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu as 2,000-pound bombs rained down on the densely packed enclave, killing more than 70,000 people. As president, Biden publicly questioned the death toll numbers. “Too many innocent Palestinians were killed,” he now writes, as if possessed by the passive-voice ghost of Donald Rumsfeld. Mistakes were made, indeed. In contrast with his remarkably clinical view of dead Gazans, he writes movingly about his friendship with Netanyahu, recalling his farewell to the prime minister days before leaving the White House: “I still love you, pal.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto games have never shied away from satirizing life, and GTA 6 has plenty of digs at famous brands, trends, and people. Not even gaming is immune to GTA's patented satire, especially if you're playing on Xbox, because there's no escape from PlayStation — or its legally distinct cousin, the JoySystem. Early in GTA 6, you'll get to bond with Jason's best pal, Cal. After maximizing the energy of Jason's bachelor pad with a little feng shui redecorating, the duo settles in for a night of booze, drugs, and video games on Booby's JoyStation console, which looks very similar to a PS5. It looks like this is the only gaming hardware in Leonida, since there are no Xbox Egg-Cube Stations X to play games on. The JoySystem isn't just for decoration either; after you've hung out with Bobby, you can return and play games on it. You can choose between an avant-garde experience or more immediate gratification with a pair of shooter games, and it's impressive how good these three games are on their own. From top-down action to stunning mystery that pokes fun at auteur-driven games, they're worth checking out. The JoySystem interface is also a 1:1 copy of the PS5 user interface, with the exact same layout for games and other apps — but given how much Sony is making from GTA 6 sales, we're guessing the tech giant sees it as a cheeky little homage. But the controllers for the console? They look terrible: Eww. In real life, PS5 sales have absolutely dominated GTA 6 preorders and sales. Video game research company Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 sales have reached 24.58 million total units via pre-purchases and copies sold at launch, which works out to about $2.36 billion in gross revenue. Of that number, 18.44 million units are remarked to be PS5 copies of the game, of which Sony will get a 30% cut of sales. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

  • It seems that Sullivan got what he wanted: In a video posted to Instagram, Sullivan remarked he was given a role in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that remember in the closing days of 2023, when Rockstar dropped the first trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6? Amidst the everything it had going on was a brief shot of a man with extensive facial tattoos, who was rapidly called out by people hip to such things as a knockoff of Florida Joker, aka Lawrence Sullivan, a Florida man who went viral for his 2017 mug shot.

Sullivan himself called it out in a since-deleted TikTok video, first telling Rockstar "we gotta talk" and then, with no response forthcoming, threatening legal action. Not long after that, though, he put forth a new offer: "Let me voice the character, give me more storyline in the game… Let's make history happen, man.".

It seems that Sullivan got what he wanted: In a video posted to Instagram, Sullivan remarked he was given a role in GTA 6.

It has been revealed that "I'm an official voice actor on GTA 6, the game." Sullivan indicates. "For the last three years a lot of people were saying I was not going to be in the game, I was not going to be nothing, they were destroying my mental health. They were saying a lot of fucked shit. But now it's time for me to shit on them and show them what the fuck Florida Joker is about!".

It has been revealed that "Y'all gonna see. Special voice actor for GTA 6. This ain't no gimmick, this ain't no lie!".

A post shared by Florida joker 🃏 (@floridaajoker).

I had doubts, but this apparently really ain't no gimmick or lie. Rockstar has posted the full GTA 6 credits and sure enough, Lawrence Sullivan is in there. Now, it could be a different Lawrence Sullivan, sure, but under the circumstances I don't think that's very likely.

Sullivan's role doesn't appear to be a particularly prominent one: He's credited, along with a great many other people, as one of "The Local Population." But at the end of the day, he made it: Florida Joker really is in GTA 6, and he seems pretty chuffed about it. I'd call that a happy ending.

Grand Theft Auto 6 contains a few fresh interesting pieces of evidence that seem to indicate Rockstar’s popular crime-sim franchise lives in the same universe as its also-popular cowboy series, Red Dead Redemption.

Let’s start with one of the most compelling and obvious connections between GTA 6 and Red Dead: a book you can find in the new game that directly references events from RDR 2. As spotted and shared online by GameRoll, there’s a book players can find early on in Brian’s Marina in GTA 6 that contains many references to both Red Dead Redemption and its prequel, Red Dead Redemption 2. For example, the book mentions a gunslinger players can meet in RDR 2, as well as mentions of locations from those games such as Blackwater and New Austin.

Iâm pleasantly surprised that Rockstar has clearly merged the RDR and GTA universes (I go into an easter egg here so donât read if you donât wanna).

This book in Brianâs Marina has MULTIPLE references to RDR1 and RDR2. It describes the demise of outlaw Flaco Hernandez, who isâ¦ pic.twitter.com/J3xecySXL0.

— GameRoll (@GameRoll_) November 20, 2026.

A more subtle connection, but one that has some interesting implications, can be randomly spotted on the license plates of some cars in GTA 6. Every so often, you might spot a car with a Upcoming Austin license plate. In the world of Red Dead, New Austin is intended to be the game’s version of Texas. Things get a bit weird if you think about all of this too much, as Texas has been mentioned in both franchises before. But then again, GTA V mentions Florida, which has been retconned into Leonida in GTA 6. So this stuff happens sometimes.

It has been revealed that A sillier connection to Red Dead can be spotted at a western-themed mini-golf course in GTA 6. If you explore that place, you’ll rapidly discover a small dog with a cowboy doll attached to his back. Look closer, and you’ll be able to identify that cowboy as Arthur Morgan.

Found a familiar friend on âhorsebackâ byu/Scholsey01 inGTA6.

And speaking of Arthur Morgan, you can actually find what looks a lot like his famous hat in GTA 6, as well. It’s the hat I wear when I go hunting as Jason. Before all this, people spotted connections between RDR2 and GTA 6 in pre-release trailers and screenshots. Some of these connections were also spotted in GTA V, like a president from RDR being featured in artwork.

So does this all mean that GTA 6 is in the same universe as Red Dead Redemption 2? I think it clearly indicates that Rockstar is playing around with that idea. The problem is that if you dig into the lore of both franchises, you’ll find some discrepancies. But Rockstar has shown in the past that it’s willing to simply retcon these kinds of complications without feeling the need to explain anything.
